rawCommits.subject: fix(agents): throttle permission heal logs and PUT shadow upstream
rawCommits.body:
When aura-network returns an empty `permissions` bundle on an agent
GET, `reconcile_permissions_with_shadow` rescues the in-memory view
from the local shadow. That safety net was firing on every list/get
refresh (frequent sidebar polling), producing a WARN per agent per
cycle and never doing anything to stop the drift upstream.

Add a per-process dedup set on `AgentService` so the WARN log fires
at most once per agent per boot, and on that first encounter spawn a
best-effort PUT that pushes the shadow value back to aura-network so
subsequent GETs can round-trip cleanly. The PUT fails soft (no
network client, no JWT, no tokio runtime, or upstream rejection all
short-circuit silently) and the shadow adoption still runs on every
reconcile call regardless of dedup state — only the log + outbound
write are throttled.

`UpdateAgentRequest` gains a `Default` derive so the heal call can
construct a "permissions-only" partial update via struct-update
syntax without listing every other optional field.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: throttle permission heal logs and PUT shadow upstream

rawCommits.subject: feat(dev-loop): derive TaskKind at health-gate time from task description
rawCommits.body:
Replaces the conservative `TaskScope::default()` + `TaskKind::Unknown`
fallback in `maybe_run_health_gate` with a real derivation pass: the
gate now fetches the task description from storage and runs it through
`extract_task_scope` + `classify_task_kind` so doc/refactor/verify
tasks in a red workspace correctly route to `UnchangedAdvisory`
(permissive) or `RedBlockedByStrictMode` (strict) instead of always
hitting `RedBlockingImplementation`.

This closes the only behavioral gap from the original
workspace-health-diff-gate plan (#4 in the original 8-item todo list):
the `TaskKind` classifier was shipped in Phase 1 but never wired into
the live gate. Until now, the AURA_BLOCK_TASK_DONE_ON_ANY_WORKSPACE_RED
knob was effectively dead code in production because every task hit
the `Implementation | Unknown` arm of `classify_delta` before strict
mode was even checked.

* `classify_task_for_gate(description)` -> `(TaskScope, TaskKind)` is
  extracted as a pure helper so the classification step is
  unit-testable without an `AppState` or storage fake, and so the
  fallback path (no description fetched) shares the exact same shape
  as the happy path.
* `fetch_task_description` is a best-effort storage read: any failure
  (no JWT, no storage client, storage error) silently falls back to an
  empty description, which `classify_task_for_gate` maps to
  `TaskKind::Unknown` - preserving the pre-Phase-5a "never loosen the
  gate on transient storage issues" contract.
* 5 inline tests pin the four kinds the verdict matrix branches on
  (Documentation, Refactor, Verification, Implementation) plus the
  empty-description Unknown fallback.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-input): stop centered wrapper jitter at the wrap boundary
rawCommits.body:
A prompt that wrapped at single-line padding-right (~220px reserve) but
fit at multi-line padding-right (32px) caused the input bar to bounce
between single- and multi-line layouts on every frame. The act of
entering multi-line widened the textarea, the prompt then fit on one
line, the existing multi -> single anti-oscillation would land just
under threshold on sub-pixel rounding, the picker re-appeared inline,
the textarea narrowed, the prompt re-wrapped, etc.

In the docked state only the inner container's top edge moves so the
oscillation is barely visible, but .inputWrapperCentered anchors with
`bottom: 50%; transform: translateY(50%)` and grows symmetrically
around its center, so the ~44px height delta becomes a fast up/down
shift of the entire bar in the empty-thread / centered state. Pressing
space pushes the prompt past the wide-layout wrap boundary, both
measurements then agree on multi-line, and the cycle stops.

Mirror the existing multi -> single anti-oscillation in the single ->
multi direction: only enter multi-line when the prompt still wraps at
the wider multi-line `padding-right: 32px`. If the wide layout fits on
one line, stay single-line - the textarea still autogrows to show the
wrapped second line at the narrow width, but the picker, info bar, and
wrapper height all stay stable.

Adds a boundary regression test that stubs scrollHeight to wrap only
at narrow padding-right and asserts the picker stays inline (no flip
to the bottom-chrome row) on the initial render.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(projects): make Orbit repo creation failures non-fatal
rawCommits.body:
Previously, any failure from Orbit's POST /v1/repos (including the
transient "failed to initialize repository storage" 500 from an
exhausted-rootfs Orbit deploy) would roll back the freshly created
project and fail the request, leaving users unable to start new
projects while Orbit was unhealthy.

Coupling project creation to a third-party service's transient
availability is the wrong default. Switch to best-effort: log a
warning and keep the project. Recovery is automatic because
OrbitClient::ensure_repo treats 409 as success, so the next caller
(dev-loop push, manual re-attach via update_project, etc.) will
silently create the repo once Orbit recovers. The push path still
classifies and surfaces Orbit-down as remote_storage_exhausted /
push_deferred via the existing ENOSPC runbook UX, so the user still
gets a clear "Orbit is unhealthy" signal -- just at push time.

Applies to both create_project_impl and the update_project
"first-time Orbit attach" branch for consistency.

rawCommits.subject: fix(harness): fall back to SWARM_BASE_URL for local harness URL
rawCommits.body:
Building on the previous commit's preflight: the actual production
unblock for aura.ai chat is to make local_harness_base_url() resolve
through SWARM_BASE_URL when LOCAL_HARNESS_URL is unset, instead of
defaulting to loopback. The deployed aura-node Render service serves
both the LocalHarness /stream WS and the SwarmHarness HTTP API on the
same port, so an env that already has SWARM_BASE_URL set is enough to
power chat too -- no Render dashboard change required.

Resolution order, codified in crates/aura-os-harness/src/harness_url.rs:

  1. LOCAL_HARNESS_URL  (explicit operator override -- still wins when
     chat sessions should target a different upstream than the swarm
     gateway).
  2. SWARM_BASE_URL     (the same aura-node already serves both
     protocols; one env var, two jobs).
  3. http://localhost:<channel-port>  (dev-only default; production
     should never land here).

resolve_local_harness_base_url + ResolvedHarnessUrl + HarnessUrlSource
are now public so the boot-time preflight in aura-os-server reuses the
same logic instead of duplicating it. The preflight's misconfigured
arm fires only when both env vars are unset/loopback (i.e. resolution
fell through to the localhost default), which matches the bug shape
that produced the outage. A new info!-level boot line stamps the
resolved URL and the env var it came from so on-call can confirm the
fallback at a glance.

Tests:
- crates/aura-os-harness/src/harness_url.rs gains 6 unit tests for the
  resolution matrix (explicit wins, swarm fallback, blank-string
  rejection, localhost default, slash trimming, source naming).
- apps/aura-os-server/src/app_builder/harness_autospawn.rs preflight
  tests are extended with the SWARM_BASE_URL-fallback case and the
  loopback-via-SWARM_BASE_URL misconfig case, and the existing tests
  are updated for the new struct-variant enum shape carrying url+source.

Docs: docs/render-deployment.md now describes the resolution order
and reflects that LOCAL_HARNESS_URL is optional in prod when
SWARM_BASE_URL is already pointing at the deployed aura-node.

rawCommits.subject: feat(server): spawn bundled aura-node sidecar from aura-os-server, mirroring desktop
rawCommits.body:
Render deploys could not run chat because aura-os-server's autospawn
path used `cargo run --release`, which has no Rust toolchain at
runtime, so production set `AURA_DISABLE_LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTOSPAWN=true`
and chat fell through to a localhost connect that nothing was bound
to. The desktop app already solves this exact problem by shipping a
precompiled `aura-node` binary alongside `aura-os-desktop` and
spawning it as a child process; this commit lifts the same shape
into `aura-os-server`.

Production path now matches desktop:

1. Render build clones `aura-harness` and `cargo build --release`s
   `aura-node` next to `aura-os-server` (build command updated in
   docs).
2. At startup `maybe_spawn_local_harness` first calls the new
   `try_spawn_harness_binary`, which resolves the binary via
   `AURA_HARNESS_BIN` or a candidate-path scan (sibling
   `aura-harness/target/release`, exe-relative locations,
   `target/release/`). When found it spawns the child, applies the
   existing `derive_harness_url_overrides` so the sidecar's
   `HttpDomainApi` posts back to this server, and stamps
   `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` to the bound URL so downstream
   `LocalHarness::from_env()` connects to the sidecar.
3. The legacy `cargo run --release` path is preserved as
   `spawn_local_harness_from_source` and only fires when no binary
   is staged — keeps `cargo run -p aura-os-server` on a fresh dev
   box working unchanged.

The previous two harness commits (preflight + 503 message + docs;
`SWARM_BASE_URL` fallback) stay in place as defence-in-depth: if the
build forgets to stage the binary, chat still works via
`SWARM_BASE_URL`; if both fail, the boot-time `error!` still names
the remediation. Updated the misconfig message to explicitly mention
dropping `AURA_DISABLE_LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTOSPAWN` as one of the
remediation levers.

Tests: 12/12 in `app_builder::harness_autospawn` pass, including new
`harness_binary_filename_matches_platform_convention` and
`resolve_harness_binary_path_respects_aura_harness_bin_when_file_exists`.
No new clippy warnings.

lightbox with every image in the conversation -- both user

rawCommits.subject: fix(dev-loop): stop rapid Stop+Start cycles wedging the AutomationBar
rawCommits.body:
Continually toggling the dev automation run could leave the play
button's progress ring spinning forever with no task output and no
way to recover other than restarting both harness and app. The
harness was still healthy; the wedge was on the server.

Three server-side fixes (all in dev_loop/), plus a client-side
safety-net hydrate so the unified spinner snaps to authoritative
state after every Start / Resume / Stop:

1. Synchronous LoopEnded on Stop.
   `abort_and_remove` now stashes Arc<LoopHandle> on
   `ActiveAutomaton` and calls `mark_cancelled().await` BEFORE
   aborting the forwarder task. Previously the only path to
   LoopEnded was the Drop impl on the forwarder's clone, which
   fires after the forwarder unwinds; that delay let a rapid
   follow-up Start's LoopOpened land on the client ahead of the
   late LoopEnded, leaving the activity store anchored to a stale
   loop instance.

2. Explicit ws-reader cancellation on Stop.
   `ActiveAutomaton` now also holds a `WsReaderHandle` clone. Stop
   calls `cancel()` on it so the harness ws-slot semaphore
   releases immediately rather than waiting for the forwarder task
   to drop the last clone on its way out -- which under back-to-
   back Stop+Start cycles could pin the harness slot.

3. Freshness gate on the adopt-shortcut.
   The `loop_started` reused branch in `start_loop` previously
   trusted `alive == true` alone to take the shortcut, which let
   a registry entry whose ws-reader had silently died inherit the
   reuse path forever. `last_forwarder_event_at` is now stamped on
   every harness event the forwarder consumes;
   `can_reuse_forwarder` refuses reuse if the gap exceeds 2min.
   Paused entries skip the gate (they legitimately have no
   traffic). Logic extracted into a pure
   `evaluate_forwarder_reuse` for unit testing.

Client safety net:
- `useAutomationStatus.handleStart` / Resume / `handleStopConfirm`
  call `useLoopActivityStore.hydrate({ project_id })` after the
  HTTP round-trip. The spinner store reconciles with authoritative
  server state without waiting on the legacy
  `loop_started`/`loop_stopped` WS event or the stall watchdog.
- `replaceSnapshot` learns a filter parameter so per-project
  hydrate evicts only matching rows; unfiltered (boot/reconnect)
  hydrate keeps the existing full-replace semantics. Without this
  a per-project hydrate would wipe loops in other projects.

Tests:
- New `loop_stop_publishes_loop_ended_synchronously` integration
  test pins #1: subscribes to the typed event hub, posts /stop,
  asserts LoopEnded arrives within 250ms (it cannot if the fix
  regresses back to Drop-only).
- New `dev_loop::registry::tests` unit tests pin #3: cover fresh,
  stale, paused, dead, and mismatched-automaton-id branches of
  the reuse decision against `evaluate_forwarder_reuse` directly.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: stop rapid Stop+Start cycles wedging the AutomationBar

rawCommits.subject: fix(public-chat): make sidebar '+' land on a fresh chat canvas
rawCommits.body:
The logged-out (and Normie-mode) sidebar's "+" button was supposed to
take the visitor to a brand-new chat surface, identical to a
first-visit landing. Two bugs made the press read as "the + button
didn't take me to a new chat screen":

1. `LoggedOutShell.handleNewChat` minted a fresh session every time
   it was clicked. When the visitor was already sitting on an empty
   "New chat" row, the destination canvas was indistinguishable from
   the one they were already looking at — clicking + just appended
   another orphan "New chat" row to the sidebar without any visible
   effect on the chat surface. Dedupe so the press reuses the most
   recent zero-turn session if one already exists; only fall through
   to `createSession()` when every session has at least one turn.

2. `usePublicChat` kept the input draft, isStreaming flag,
   sourceImage, error banner, and in-flight SSE handles in component-
   local React state that survived `sessionId` flips. Switching
   sessions (via "+", row click, or any `?session=` change) carried
   those values forward, so the destination canvas looked like the
   same chat the visitor just left. Add a streamKey-keyed reset in
   the existing `useEffect`: on every flip, close any open handles
   and clear the per-session view state. Skipped on the very first
   run (matched-streamKey case) so an in-flight send isn't clobbered
   mid-mount.

Adds two regression tests in `LoggedOutShell.test.tsx` (empty-session
reuse vs. fresh mint) and one in `use-public-chat.test.tsx` (state
reset on streamKey flip) that pin both contracts.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: make sidebar '+' land on a fresh chat canvas

rawCommits.subject: fix(sidekick-run): preserve failed task history in the Run pane
rawCommits.body:
When a task in the sidekick automation Run pane failed before any
text_delta / tool result had landed (early API timeout,
completion-gate rejection, silent task_failed), the row immediately
collapsed to the generic "Task failed without producing output."
empty state and lost every signal the user had been watching in the
live cooking indicator (progress label, thinking text, partial
buffer, failure reason).

Root cause: finalizeStream's "shouldPersistTurn" gate only emitted
an event into the events array when a non-empty buffer or
unsnapshotted tool calls were present, so a no-content failed
terminal left events.length === 0. snapshotTaskTurns then bailed on
its own empty-events guard, the task-turn-cache stayed empty, and
CompletedTaskOutput fell through to the empty-state copy.

Force finalizeStream to always emit a synthetic assistant-message
event for reason="failed" carrying the failure message in
errorMessage (falling back to "task failed without a reason from
the harness" when none is supplied) and folding the live progress
label captured by task-stream-bootstrap into content when no text
ever streamed. Behaviour for reason="completed" / "disconnected" is
unchanged, so clean no-op completions still render as a bare
header.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: preserve failed task history in the Run pane

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-input): break model-picker oscillation at the wrap boundary
rawCommits.body:
At specific prompt lengths the textarea's content width sits right on
the wrap boundary between the single-line `padding-right: min(220px,
42%)` reserve and the multi-line `padding-right: 32px` reserve. The
existing anti-oscillation predictions in `autoResize` re-measure with
inline `padding-right` overrides, but at the boundary the simulation
can disagree with the actual layout by a sub-pixel because it only
mimics one side effect of the `data-multiline` swap (it doesn't
reproduce the `.inputRowEnd display: none`, `.inputRow position:
static`, or the `containerBottom` row insertion). When the prediction
lands on the wrong side of the threshold, every `ResizeObserver` fire
that's caused by our own state toggle re-evaluates and reverses the
toggle, and the picker bounces inline<->footer forever. In the
centered empty-thread state this is visible as a fast vertical jitter
of the entire input bar (`bottom: 50%; transform: translateY(50%)`
amplifies the ~44px height delta around the wrapper midline).

Add a one-shot transition lockout in `InputBarShell`: every time
`autoResize` actually toggles `isMultiLine`, arm a counter that the
next `ResizeObserver` callback consumes by running a height-only
update (new `applyHeightOnly` helper) instead of the full `autoResize`.
The fire that's a consequence of our own CSS swap can no longer undo
the toggle. Real width changes (window resize, sidebar collapse, panel
resize) still go through the `window` `resize` handler or a
subsequent `ResizeObserver` fire after the lockout disarms, so they
keep getting a full re-evaluation.

Adds a regression test that installs a `ResizeObserver` mock and an
asymmetric `scrollHeight` stub where the narrow simulation lies about
wrap state. Without the lockout the manual `ResizeObserver` fire
flips the picker back to the inline slot; with the lockout the
picker stays in the bottom chrome row.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: break model-picker oscillation at the wrap boundary

rawCommits.subject: perf(sessions): drop N+1 events probe; storage filters event_count>0
rawCommits.body:
The chat-app session list (Chats sidekick, projects sidekick, chat-app left panel) was slow on accounts with chat history because filter_nonempty_sessions ran one list_events?limit=1 HTTP probe per session on every list call. For a project with A agents and N sessions: 1 + A + N round-trips per page open.

Move the empty-row filter into aura-storage where it is a single indexed query. Companion migration 0014 in aura-storage adds event_count and last_event_at columns on sessions, maintained by an AFTER INSERT trigger on session_events, plus partial indexes WHERE event_count > 0.

aura-os-server: StorageSession exposes the new columns; new StorageClient::list_project_sessions hits the new GET /api/projects/:project_id/sessions endpoint; list_project_sessions and list_sessions are pass-throughs; filter_nonempty_sessions deleted; mock storage mirrors the filter and ordering.
Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: perf(sessions): gate lazy /summarize on row visibility
rawCommits.body:
useSessionSummaries used to fire one POST /sessions/:id/summarize per untitled session as soon as the list mounted. Each call loads the full event transcript and round-trips Haiku, so on an account with many legacy untitled sessions the first paint of the Chats sidekick triggered N parallel LLM calls — most for rows the user never scrolls to.

Wire an IntersectionObserver per SessionRowButton (rootMargin 200px so titles land just before the row enters the viewport) and forward visibility into useSessionSummaries via a visibleSessionIds set. Off-screen rows are now skipped; the on-send title path (generate_session_title) still pre-titles new sessions so the gate only affects pre-existing untitled rows.

Hook keeps backward compat: undefined/null visibleSessionIds falls back to the legacy summarize-everything behavior.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: perf(sessions): gate lazy /summarize on row visibility

rawCommits.subject: perf(sessions): collapse chat-app cross-agent fan-out to single /api/me/sessions call
rawCommits.body:
Wires up the chat-app left panel to the user-scoped session list endpoint added in aura-storage migration 0015. The panel used to fan out one /api/projects/:p/agents/:a/sessions call per (agent, project_binding) pair on first paint -- for a user with A agents and B average bindings each, that was A x (1 + B) HTTP calls before any rows could render. With this change it's 1 (plus a sibling listProjectBindings call for the chat agent that the new-chat ' + ' button still needs).

Wire types + client:

- New StorageEnrichedSession (StorageSession + agent_id) mirroring the EnrichedSession shape aura-storage returns. agent_name and project_name are deliberately absent: project_agents has no name column, and aura-storage owns no projects table -- the FE resolves both from its existing per-agent and per-project caches.

- StorageClient::list_my_sessions(jwt) calls GET /api/me/sessions. Honours AURA_STORAGE_TEST_USER_ID (appended as ?user=<id>) so the in-memory mock can scope to a user without real auth; production sets neither and aura-storage's JWT extractor is the sole authority on user_id.

- Mock storage (aura-os-storage testutil) gains a list_my_sessions handler. Ownership lives in MockStorageDb.session_users -- a side map populated by tests after seeding sessions, since the mock has no JWT to derive created_by from.

Domain + handler:

- New aura_os_core::EnrichedSession (Session + agent_id: Option<AgentId>). storage_enriched_session_to_enriched_session in aura-os-sessions reuses storage_session_to_session for the inner Session and parses the joined agent_id; malformed agent_id strings drop to None rather than poison the row.

- New aura-os-server handler list_my_sessions: pass-through to StorageClient::list_my_sessions, mapped through the conversion fn. Registered at /api/me/sessions.

Frontend:

- sessionsApi.listMySessions() returns EnrichedSession[].

- New userSessionsSurfaceKey() singleton + loadUserSessions store action: single fetch, annotates rows with _projectId / _agentInstanceId / _agentId / _projectName (project name resolved from useProjectsListStore.projects since the wire shape omits it). Preserves the applyPendingSummariesToList / preservePendingRows story so optimistic placeholders and SessionReady-swap races still survive a refetch.

- New loadAgentBindings store action: bindings-only refresh that doesn't fan out the per-binding session calls. The chat-app left panel calls it for the chat agent so the ' + ' button's ceoHomeProjectId lookup still resolves; we no longer trigger loadAgentSessions for that purpose because it would re-introduce the fan-out we just collapsed.

- ChatAppLeftPanel.tsx: agents.forEach(loadAgentSessions) replaced with a single loadUserSessions() effect. agentByInstanceId map (built by walking bindingsByAgent for every agent) replaced with a template-id keyed agentsByTemplateId map and a resolveSessionAgent that reads target._agentId from the row. Surface keys for delete/restore/error all collapse onto the single user-sessions surface.

- useChatAppSessions hook simplified to a straight surface read; the per-agent flat-and-resort logic is gone now that the server returns a pre-merged list.

The IntersectionObserver-gated useSessionSummaries from the prior commit on this branch still applies: rows that scroll into view are the only ones that get a /summarize round-trip, so the new single-fetch list never triggers an N+1 burst on mount.

Tests:

- Extends apps/aura-os-server/tests/session_list_empty_filter_test.rs with list_my_sessions_returns_only_users_sessions: stamps two users' sessions in the mock, verifies the endpoint only returns the requesting user's non-empty sessions.

- New build_test_app_with_storage_db helper in tests/common/mod.rs surfaces the mock SharedDb so tests can poke session_users directly. The existing build_test_app_with_storage signature is unchanged so the other ~12 callers continue to compile.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(stores): break sessions->projects->auth TDZ cycle at boot
rawCommits.body:
Commit 1e8834e0e added a static
`import { useProjectsListStore } from "./projects-list-store"` to
`sessions-list-store.ts` so the new `loadUserSessions` action could
look up project names client-side. That import unintentionally closed
a circular module-init loop that put `useAuthStore` in the Temporal
Dead Zone:

  auth-store
    -> event-store (re-exports event-store/event-store)
    -> engine-event-handlers
    -> sessions-list-store
    -> projects-list-store
    -> useAuthStore.subscribe(...)  <- at module top level (line 517)

`projects-list-store.ts` calls `useAuthStore.subscribe(...)` at module
top level, so it forces `auth-store` to be evaluated before its own
`export const useAuthStore = create(...)` line has executed. The
result was a hard-stop boot crash:

  Uncaught ReferenceError: Cannot access 'useAuthStore' before
  initialization

surfaced by the splash-screen fallback in `interface/index.html`.

Fix is surgical: drop the static import and inline a dynamic
`await import("./projects-list-store")` at the single use site
(line 567 inside `loadUserSessions`, an async action that already
awaits a network call so the extra microtask is free in practice).
The dynamic import is resolved well after both stores have finished
their top-level initialization, breaking the cycle without changing
behaviour. Added a module-top comment documenting the cycle and a
sibling comment at the call site pointing back at it so the next
person who tries to "clean up" the dynamic import has the context
they need not to.

Tests:
- src/stores/sessions-list-store.test.tsx -> 33/33 pass
- src/stores/auth-store.test.ts -> 25/25 pass
- src/stores/projects-list-store.test.ts -> 25/25 pass
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(routing): redirect orphaned URLs to / when toggling into normie shell
rawCommits.body:
The Normie/Advanced toggle (`ModeToggle` in the sidebar) only mutates
`useUIModeStore`; it does NOT navigate. That is correct for the
Advanced -> Advanced case (every app route in the registry stays
reachable) and for the Normie -> Normie case (only `/` and `/chat`
exist either way).

But when a user is sitting on a deep advanced URL like
`/projects/:id/agents/:id` and flips to Normie, the `<Routes>` block
re-renders with only the normie-shell branch (`/` index and `/chat`).
Neither matches the current URL, so React Router renders nothing and
logs:

  No routes matched location "/projects/.../agents/..."

The screen goes blank until the user manually navigates somewhere.

Add a `<Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/" replace />} />` to
the inNormieShell branch so the toggle always lands on the public
chat surface regardless of the URL the user came from. The redirect
is `replace` so the broken URL doesn't pollute history.

Mirrors the same `<Route path="*" .../>` catch-all that already
exists in the logged-out marketing branch, so the two unauthenticated
shells now have identical behaviour for unmatched routes.

rawCommits.subject: fix(sessions): fall back to legacy per-agent fan-out when aura-storage 404s
rawCommits.body:
The aura-os-side perf commits 19f5203ad + 1e8834e0e collapsed the
chat/projects session list down to a single indexed call against new
aura-storage endpoints (`/api/projects/:p/sessions`,
`/api/me/sessions`) that ship with migrations 0014 + 0015 in the
aura-storage repo. Those migrations exist on the aura-storage side
but have not been pushed to origin/main yet, so `aura-storage.onrender.com`
still 404s those routes.

Result on a live aura-os-server (local or any environment pointing
at the current Render deploy of aura-storage): every
`loadProjectSessions(projectId)` from the FE bubbles up as a
`status: 404 storage_error` and lights up `console.error("Failed
to load project sessions", err)` in the dev tools.

Fix: in `list_project_sessions`, match on the upstream status. The
fast-path call stays unchanged; ONLY a 404 trips the new
`list_project_sessions_legacy` fallback, which restores the
pre-19f5203ad implementation verbatim:

  1. `list_project_agents(project_id)` -> list of project agents
  2. `list_sessions(agent.id)` per agent (sequential loop, mirrors
     the pre-perf code; not parallelized so the fallback's network
     pressure is identical to what was running before the perf
     commit)
  3. `filter_nonempty_sessions_legacy` drops orphan rows with a
     `list_events?limit=1` probe per session (fail-open: probe
     errors keep the row so a transient storage hiccup never makes
     a real chat disappear)
  4. Client-side sort by `started_at DESC`

The fallback becomes dormant the instant the matching aura-storage
commits are pushed and Render rolls them out -- the fast path stops
404ing and `list_project_sessions_legacy` never runs again. No
permanent perf hit, no FE change required.

Other upstream errors (5xx, network failures, non-404 client
errors) still bubble through `map_storage_error` so genuine outages
keep surfacing the correct status to the caller; only the specific
"this endpoint does not exist yet" 404 trips the fallback.

Companion fallback for `/api/me/sessions` (chat-app left panel) is
NOT included here -- the server cannot enumerate a user's agents
without going through aura-network, so the fallback for that
surface has to live on the FE. Add it the moment we observe the
chat-app left panel hitting the same 404 path.

Tests:
- `cargo test -p aura-os-server --test session_list_empty_filter_test`
  -> 3/3 pass (fast path still works against the mock, which has
  the new endpoint)
- `cargo check -p aura-os-server` clean
- No new clippy warnings in the changed region.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(mode-toggle): stretch segments so the selection pill fills the chrome
rawCommits.body:
The shared `SlidingPills` `.root` sets `align-items: center` on the
flex container, so without `align-self: stretch` the ModeToggle
segments collapsed to just their content height (font-size +
line-height = 12px). The sliding indicator is sized from the active
segment's bounding rect, so it shrank with them — leaving a tiny
selection pill floating inside the now-38px chrome strip.

Adding `align-self: stretch` on `.segment` makes each segment fill
the pill's full inner height (`pill-height - 2*2px padding`), which
in turn lets the indicator paint the full segment cell as expected.
The base `SlidingPills` is shared with the chat input's
`ModeSelector`, so this stays scoped to the ModeToggle's own
segment override.

rawCommits.subject: refactor(ui-mode): consolidate Normie/Advanced into Simple/Advanced/Public
rawCommits.body:
Phase 1 of the AuraShell unification plan. Collapses the parallel
app-mode-store into a single 3-way ui-mode-store, renames Normie
to Simple everywhere, and removes the orphan SimpleShell + Simple
text button so the sidebar ModeToggle is the single mode switcher.

- ui-mode-store: UIMode = "simple" | "advanced" | "public" string
  literal union (no enum, no any). readPersistedMode validates
  localStorage at the boundary, migrates legacy "normie" -> "simple"
  and one-shot reads + clears legacy aura-app-mode -> aura-ui-mode.
  selectEffectiveMode(state, isAuthenticated) derives the runtime
  mode (logged-out -> public; logged-in "public" -> "simple").
- ModeToggle: ITEMS = [{ simple, Simple }, { advanced, Advanced }],
  with ToggleMode = Exclude<UIMode, "public"> so the toggle can
  never write the public sentinel.
- DesktopTitlebar: Simple text button + useAppModeStore import
  removed.
- AppShell: ResponsiveShell drops the SimpleShell branch; the
  WelcomeModal/OnboardingChecklist gate flips to mode === "advanced".
- e2e seeds switched from aura-app-mode to aura-ui-mode.
- app-mode-store.ts and views/SimpleShell/ deleted (no dead code).

Verification: typecheck clean, focused vitest (ui-mode-store +
ModeToggle + LoggedOutShell) 26/26 passing, no remaining
useAppModeStore importers, no remaining "normie" string outside
the explicit migration path.

Phase 2 (public theming) and Phase 3 (AuraShell unification)
follow.

DesktopShell + LoggedOutShell trees with one AuraShell mounted
once. Mode flips swap slot subtree contents inside stable wrappers;
no more shell-level remount, no more component identity churn,
no more search-input or ModeToggle-pill state loss across flips.

New components (interface/src/components/AuraShell/):
- AuraShell.tsx: root layout, reads useEffectiveMode() once,
  mounts BackgroundLayer + AuraTitlebar + AuraSidebar + <main>
  with <Outlet /> + BottomTaskbar exactly once. Sets data-ui-mode
  on the root for CSS gating. Sidekick lane mounts only when
  authed (right edge, doesn't shift main).
- AuraTitlebar.tsx: single ShellTitlebar instance with conditional
  leading/trailing slot children (Org+Menu/UpdatePill+Credits in
  authed; mobile menu/Theme+Login+Signup in public).
- AuraSidebar.tsx: single Lane (storageKey "aura-sidebar",
  defaultWidth 200, maxWidth 600). One sidebarHeader div mounting

    advanced -> AuthedSidebarBody (active-app LeftPanel)
    simple   -> AuthedSidebarBody (Phase 4 will pin ChatApp)
    public   -> PublicSidebarBody (LoggedOutSessionsPanel +

  Publishes --aura-sidebar-width + --left-panel-width via
  ResizeObserver on the Lane ref.
- AuraTitlebar.tsx and AuraSidebar.tsx are private co-located
  subcomponents (matching the deleted DesktopTitlebar precedent).

Stores:
- stores/sidebar-search-store.ts: keyed sidebar search query so
  the input value persists across Simple/Advanced/Public flips.
- stores/use-effective-mode.ts: useEffectiveMode() = derived
  selectEffectiveMode(state, isAuthenticated). Single source of
  truth for chrome.

Slot conditional content (DOM-stable wrappers):
- BottomTaskbar({ mode: UIMode }): always renders outer .bar so
  --shell-chrome-outer-height is reserved in every mode. In
  public, suppresses .left and .center, renders only
  ThemeToggleButton in .right.rightPrimary. Auth-required hooks
  only run in the simple/advanced branch. data-ui-mode on .bar.
- ModeToggle: aria-disabled + pointer-events:none in public,
  same SlidingPills mount, never writes "public". Forwards

as the active app whenever effectiveMode === "simple", moves
every public-chat content component into its permanent home at

folder.

- hooks/use-active-app.ts: short-circuits to ChatApp from

Each public component lands in its own folder with TSX +

monolithic LoggedOutShell.module.css is split per component;
shared rules (chat scroller, AURA video translate, radial
vignette) live in PublicChatView.module.css.

  PublicSidebarFooter from views/public-chat.

  19 files: LoggedOutShell.tsx + .module.css + .test.tsx,

Tests:

  ChatAppMainPanel; Advanced renders the active-app tree;
  Public renders PublicChatView; sign-in transition unmounts
  AgentDemoBanner + PublicSidebarFooter and mounts
  ChatAppMainPanel + ChatAppLeftPanel.
- ChatRedirectGuard.test.tsx (new): 11 cases — Simple-mode
  redirects from /projects/abc, /settings, /; passthrough on
  /chat and /chat/<id>; Advanced + public passthrough; isChatPath
  edge cases.
- use-active-app.test.tsx: +2 cases — Simple-mode pin returns

This completes the Simple/Advanced/Public unification:

rawCommits.subject: fix(public-chat): make agent demo dots bounce and morph bubble in place
rawCommits.body:
The looping AgentDemoBanner on the logged-out homepage had two
adjacent UX gaps reported during review:

  1. The three typing dots looked frozen. The bounce animation was
     defined but pitched too low to read against the dark elevated
     banner bg - 5px lift on a 6px dot with only opacity changing.
     Bumped to 7px dots, 8px lift with a 0.85->1.15 scale pulse, and
     a brightness/saturation ride on the same keyframe so the
     agent's accent color visibly flows through the three circles in
     sync with the bounce (an iMessage-style wave). Stagger is now
     400ms across a 1200ms cycle so the peaks land at a steady
     1/3-cycle cadence with no visible gap between waves.

  2. Message frames re-mounted their bubble on the typing -> content
     swap (one <div key="typing"> for the dots, a fresh
     <div key="content"> for the message), so the row's pop-open
     animation ran twice and the bubble appeared to disappear and
     come back rather than morph. Refactored to a single persistent
     bubble container for message frames: the bubble's enter
     animation runs once at row mount, and only the inner slot
     (keyed by phase) remounts on the swap, fading the dots out and
     the streaming typewriter in inside the *same* open container.
     A min-height sized to one line of text + padding keeps the
     bubble's vertical footprint constant across the swap so the
     reflow doesn't snap when the dots leave. Tool frames keep the
     shape-swap (small typing bubble -> wider tool card) since their
     visual shapes diverge too much to share a morphing container.

All existing public-chat tests still pass - the "morphs the typing
indicator into the resolved message within one row" contract
strengthens under the new structure (the bubble literally is the
same DOM element across phases now).

rawCommits.subject: fix(public-chat): stop reduced-motion from freezing the demo banner
rawCommits.body:
After the prior commit's CSS bounce + persistent-bubble refactor the
homepage hero STILL read as broken: the typing dots sat motionless
and the message text appeared in one chunk instead of streaming. The
gap was upstream of the new animation values — every per-row effect
in the demo banner was gated on `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`,
and that media query is on by default on a lot of Windows installs
(and any user who has ever toggled "Show animations in Windows" off
in accessibility settings).

The banner's file-level comment already documents an override for
the script timeline ("the demo is the entire point of the hero, so
freezing it would just leave a static empty rectangle"). That policy
applies equally to the inner animations: a dot row that doesn't
bounce and a message bubble that pops fully-typed both read as
"this UI is broken" rather than "I respect your accessibility
preference". The banner is decorative and `aria-hidden`, so the
override has no semantic impact — reduced-motion users still get
zero animation in any non-decorative surface.

Dropped:
  - `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block in
    `TypingIndicator.module.css` that pinned the dots static.
  - The runtime `matchMedia('prefers-reduced-motion: reduce')` check
    in `TypewriterText.tsx` that rendered the full message in one
    shot, plus the matching `.caret { display: none }` override.
  - All four `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` blocks in
    `AgentDemoBanner.module.css` (.demoRow, .demoBubblePhase,
    .demoMessageBubble, .demoBubbleSlot).

Updated comments on `TypingIndicator`, `TypewriterText`,
`TypewriterText.module.css`, and `AgentDemoBanner` to document the
new policy in one place and flag that any future non-decorative
consumer must add its own reduced-motion gate at the callsite.

Swapped the now-stale `TypewriterText` test that asserted the
reduced-motion shortcircuit for one that pins the opposite contract:
the stream keeps streaming even when matchMedia reports a reduce
preference.

rawCommits.subject: feat(public-chat): elegant row entrance + line-by-line terminal stream
rawCommits.body:
Two follow-up polish passes on the AgentDemoBanner now that the typing dots are bouncing and message text is streaming: 1. Row entrance was still reading as "abrupt pop-in" — 380ms / 6px slide with opacity-only fade was too clipped to register as intentional motion. Bumped to 560ms / 14px slide paired with a subtle 0.96 -> 1 scale on a near-flat ease-out-quart curve (cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1)) and anchored the transform-origin to 0% 100% so the row appears to grow from the avatar's landing spot rather than the centre of the panel. Opacity ramps in at 55% (faster than the transform) so the row is fully visible while it's still settling — the eye lands on the final pose instead of tracking a long fade tail. The scale compounds with the bubble's own pop animation for a layered entrance that feels deliberate. 2. Tool-card previews used to render the entire `
{lines}
` in one shot, which mismatched the streaming feel of the message bubbles in the same banner. Introduced `TerminalStream` (sibling to `TypingIndicator` and `TypewriterText`) — a per-line stdout-style streamer that types each line char-by-char at 14ms/char (about 2x the message typewriter, matching the bursty pace of real terminal output), rests the caret at end-of-line for 90ms, then advances to the next line. A small block caret hangs off the trailing edge of the active line throughout the stream and unmounts once the final line settles. AgentDemoBanner's tool frames now mount `` in place of the static `
`, and the legacy
     `.demoToolPreview` rules are gone — the new component owns
     its own scoped `
` styles (monospace, white-space: pre,
     overflow ellipsis) so its visual footprint inside the tool
     card is unchanged.

Implementation notes for the new component:
  - Single `useEffect` per `lines` prop holds the streaming state
    in closure (`lineIdx`/`chars` locals) and publishes snapshots
    via `setSnapshot` for re-renders. Per-char state stays out of
    the dep list so `vi.advanceTimersByTime(N)` in tests flushes
    multiple chars and lines in a single call; the earlier
    deps-in-effect-restart pattern repeatedly recreated the
    interval mid-stream and left subsequent ticks scheduled past
    the timer-advance window, which broke the per-line test
    assertions.
  - Same accessibility policy as the rest of the demo banner:
    `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` does NOT silence the stream
    (decorative homepage hero, whole banner is `aria-hidden`).
  - The new `TerminalStream` test suite pins three contracts: the
    preview starts empty (no flash of a fully-populated card on
    mount), characters reveal one at a time and the stream
    advances line-by-line in order, and the active-line caret
    unmounts once the final line completes.

All 48 public-chat unit tests pass; dist is rebuilt with the new
keyframe and component scoped class hashes verified present in
`index-*.css`.

Co-authored-by: Cursor

rawCommits.subject: feat(public-chat): backend agent, syntax highlighting, FLIP row shift
rawCommits.body:
Three coordinated polish passes on the homepage AgentDemoBanner:

  1. Added a Backend agent (amber accent #fbbf24, Database icon) and
     extended SCRIPT with four new frames between the Frontend's
     edit_file and bash build: a backend "wiring the endpoint and
     migration in parallel" message, a typed TS API route
     (api/pricing.ts using a zod schema and an express handler), a
     SQL migration (CREATE TABLE pricing_tier...) and a pytest run
     showing 8 passing tests. Polished the existing PricingTiers.tsx
     frame to a properly typed TSX snippet (interface TierProps +
     arrow component) so it gets meaningful highlighting too. The
     workflow now reads as a four-agent ship loop (architect plans,
     frontend builds, backend wires API+migration, reviewer
     approves) with ~40s wall-clock per pass (was ~22s).

  2. Syntax highlighting that tracks theme mode. Added an optional
     `language?` field on `ToolFrame` and an optional `language?`
     prop on TerminalStream. When set, each preview line is pre-
     highlighted via `hljs.highlight(line, { language })` and the
     resulting `<span class="hljs-*">` tree is flattened into a
     `{ text, className }[]` token list by a new `tokenizeLine`
     helper that walks an off-document `<template>` element
     (innermost hljs class wins so nested spans keep their
     classification). The streamer then clips the tokens to N
     visible chars per line via `clipTokens` — a keyword colored at
     character 1 stays the same color as the rest of it streams in
     (no mid-word color shift, the user-chosen "prehighlight-clip"
     approach). When `language` is omitted (or not registered with
     hljs) the component falls through to today's plain-text
     render so non-code frames like the architect's plan checklist
     and the reviewer's merge summary aren't mis-classified by the
     highlighter. Theme follows automatically — the existing
     `HighlightThemeBridge` swaps github / github-dark stylesheets
     on `useTheme().resolvedTheme` change, and `hljs-*` class names
     are global (not CSS-Module-scoped) so spans rendered by
     TerminalStream pick up the right theme on first paint and on
     every subsequent toggle. Zero new infra.

  3. FLIP (First-Last-Invert-Play) row animator so existing rows
     slide up smoothly alongside the new row's slide-in instead of
     snapping. New local `useFlipRows` hook in AgentDemoBanner
     captures each row's top via `useLayoutEffect` (keyed off the
     stable `nextKey` from the existing reducer), compares to the
     previous render, and for any row whose position changed
     applies an inverse `translateY(<delta>)` synchronously — then
     on the next animation frame transitions back to no transform
     with the same `cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1)` curve and
     540ms duration as the row enter keyframe so the new-row
     slide-in and existing-rows shift-up read as one coordinated
     motion. Sets `animation: none` before the inverse transform
     so the row enter keyframe's `fill: both` final value can't
     shadow the inline transform. Forces a reflow between the
     two style writes so the browser doesn't coalesce them into a
     no-op transition. Map sweep at the end of the effect drops
     refs / positions for keys that scrolled off the top of the
     window so the maps don't grow unbounded across loop resets.
     DemoFrameRow gains an optional `rowRef?` prop forwarded to
     its root div.

Tests:
  - Two new TerminalStream assertions: hljs-keyword spans are
    present after a `language="typescript"` stream completes
    (proves the highlight path is wired through, not falling
    through to plain text), and they're still present + correctly
    classified mid-stream when only "con" of "const" has been
    revealed (proves the clip preserves token boundaries rather
    than re-highlighting the raw prefix each tick).
  - No new useFlipRows test — jsdom's `getBoundingClientRect()`
    returns zero rects for every element so the unit-test would
    just exercise the no-op branch. Behavior is verified visually
    after the rebuilt dist reloads; `AgentDemoBanner.test.tsx`
    still pins the mount/resolve contracts that matter at the
    component level.

50 tests pass (was 48). Dist rebuilt and verified: `api/pricing`,
`Backend`, `pricing_tier`, and `terminalStream` all present in the
bundled `index-*.js` / `index-*.css`.

rawCommits.subject: fix(public-chat): stop mock DM rows from re-animating on every script advance
rawCommits.body:
`useFlipRows` was firing on every `DMWindow` re-render and applying a
480ms `translateY` transition to already-settled rows whenever ANY
window received a new frame. Symptoms: a message would load in, the
typewriter would finish, then ~1-2s later the same window's earlier
rows would visibly jump as the next agent's frame mounted elsewhere on
the desktop. Four bugs were compounding:

  1. `useLayoutEffect(..., [visibleKeys])` deps on `frames.map(f =>
     f.key)`, a fresh array reference every render — React's `Object.is`
     deps check always sees it as changed, so the effect runs on every
     re-render rather than only when frames actually change.
  2. `DMWindowManager` rebuilds `state.windows` on every `advance`, so
     every `DMWindow` re-renders on every script step (not just the one
     receiving the frame).
  3. `.dmWindow` has a continuous `dmIdleDrift` translateY animation;
     measurements via `getBoundingClientRect()` (viewport-relative,
     includes ancestor transforms) saw 1-3px deltas between renders
     even when the row's own layout was unchanged.
  4. The body auto-scroll-to-bottom lives in `useEffect`, which runs
     AFTER FLIP's `useLayoutEffect`. FLIP captured pre-scroll positions
     on render N, then on render N+1 measured POST the previous
     render's scroll and computed a ~rowHeight delta — animating every
     existing row by that delta. This was the user-visible "jump".

Delete the helper entirely and replace its intent (smooth slide as new
content is appended) with `scroll-behavior: smooth` on `.dmBody`. Rows
are only ever appended at the bottom, so their layout positions never
actually shift; the only motion that should happen is the body's
scroll-to-bottom, which the browser now animates on its own — without
re-firing on unrelated re-renders.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

most recent message ended up clipped below maxHeight until the next

rawCommits.subject: fix(public-chat): pin DM bubble display so typing -> content swap doesn't shift ~1px
rawCommits.body:
The bubble's `display` was changing between phases: the typing phase
carried `display: inline-flex; align-items: center;` via the
`.dmTypingBubble` modifier, while the content phase fell back to the
default `display: block`. Each layout model resolved the bubble's
`min-height: calc(12px + 1.4em)` (~28.1px subpixel) to a slightly
different integer pixel height, producing a residual ~1px shift on
every typing -> content swap — visible as a small jump on the
bottom-anchored `frontend_reviewer` window once the typing dots
resolved into text.

Move `display: inline-flex; align-items: center;` onto the base
`.dmBubble` so both phases share the same layout model, and drop the
now-redundant `.dmTypingBubble` class (along with its usages in
`DMWindow.tsx`). The bubble's external box height is now identical
across the swap, so the surrounding rows and the window's top edge
stay pixel-stable.

rawCommits.subject: fix(public-chat): keep streaming caret mounted so DM text doesn't 1px-shift on completion
rawCommits.body:
Unmounting the empty `inline-block` caret with `vertical-align:
text-bottom` from `TypewriterText` (and the parallel caret in
`TerminalStream`) at end-of-stream forced the surrounding line box
to recompute its baseline strut without the inline-block
contribution; the resulting subpixel rounding shifted the inline
text by ~1px the instant a DM message finished streaming. The
`.dmBubble` `min-height` floor kept the bubble's outer box stable,
so the jitter was contained to the text inside the bubble — subtle
but consistent.

Both carets now stay mounted at completion and toggle a
`.caretHidden` modifier (`visibility: hidden; animation: none;`)
instead, which keeps the inline-block in the line and holds the
line metrics byte-identical across the streaming -> complete
transition. The carets also expose `data-state="blinking" |
"hidden"` so the unit tests can pin the on/off contract without
relying on hashed CSS module class names.

rawCommits.subject: feat(public-chat): expand-out + staggered-collapse mock DM windows
rawCommits.body:
The empty-state hero now animates the DM cascade in and out instead
of mounting / unmounting bare elements:

- Open: each window's chrome scales up from 0.4 to 1 with a small
  upward translate over 500ms (`dmWindowExpand`). Body rows are
  gated behind an `isOpen` flag that flips after `WINDOW_OPEN_MS`,
  so the typewriter / typing-indicator timers don't tick against a
  scaling parent (which used to chew through the first message's
  reveal while the window was still settling).
- Close: when the script finishes, the manager holds the final
  frame for a 2.4s dwell, then dispatches `beginClose` and every
  window plays `dmWindowCollapse` (ease-in, 360ms, scale 1 -> 0.4).
  Windows tear down in reverse z-order (most-recently focused
  first) with a 120ms stagger between each via inline
  `animation-delay`. The manager then waits the longest close
  (`WINDOW_CLOSE_MS + (n - 1) * STAGGER`) before dispatching
  `reset` so the loop restart doesn't yank away mid-animation.

Manager lifecycle is now a three-step chain (advance -> dwell ->
beginClose -> wait for staggered closes -> reset) with a new
`phase: "running" | "closing"` state and `beginClose` action. The
phase also gates `advance` so stray timers can't mutate the
collapsing cascade.

rawCommits.subject: refactor(public-chat): radically simplify persona swap to fade-out -> swap -> fade-in
rawCommits.body:
The cross-fade + decode-gate + onLoad-gate stack still produced visible seams on persona swaps. Replace the whole thing with a plain sequential fade: fade the current persona out, swap the committed snapshot once it's invisible, fade the new persona in. State machine ------------- `PublicChatView` now keeps just two persona pointers: - `activeIndex`: the visitor's last click, drives everything that should feel responsive (rail aria-current, foreground vars, CTA glow, chat palette base color). - `committedIndex`: the persona currently painted on the bg + wallpaper, lags by exactly `FADE_MS` (220ms). A single derived boolean `visible = activeIndex === committedIndex` drives the opacity of both surfaces. While the two indices disagree, `visible` is `false` and the CSS opacity transition on each wrapper tweens 1 -> 0. A `setTimeout(FADE_MS)` then flips `committedIndex` to match `activeIndex`; the same render makes `visible` true again so the wrapper transitions 0 -> 1 over the new content, which is now in the DOM at opacity 0. Wallpaper + color as one element -------------------------------- The desktop background inside `MockAuraApp` is now a single `.desktopBackground` `
` that paints the persona's `desktopBackgroundColor` on itself AND holds the wallpaper `` as its only child. The parent toggles this single wrapper's opacity via the new `desktopBackgroundOpacity` prop (forwarded through `ComposePanel`), so color and image always dissolve together as one snapshot - no separate layers that could snap relative to each other. Same on the page bg: one `.siteBackground` wrapper that carries the color and the inner ``. Removed ------- - `cross-fade.ts` (`useCrossFadeLayers` hook + outgoing/entering layered state machine) - no longer needed; both surfaces use a single element with a plain CSS opacity transition. - `cross-fade.module.css` (the `.layerEntering` / `.layerLeaving` / `.layerLeavingFading` keyframe classes). - `persona-preload.ts` (`useDecodedPersonaIndex` decode gate) - the fade-out window naturally hides any one-frame paint lag on the new image, so we don't need to gate the commit on `Image.decode()` resolving. - The corresponding `HTMLImageElement.prototype.decode` test polyfill that only existed to keep the decode gate pass-through under jsdom. Kept ---- - The GPU-resident `.preloadStash` block in `PublicChatView`. With the simpler swap model the new image still needs to be paint-ready when the fade-in kicks in; persistently-mounted hidden `` elements keep every persona's bitmap warm in the browser's image cache so the visible wrapper never paints over an empty layer mid-tween. Co-authored-by: Cursor

rawCommits.subject: style(public-chat): make persona swap fade more obvious
rawCommits.body:
Stretches the persona swap window so the fade-out -> blank -> fade-in
sequence is clearly readable. Three changes, all driven by one number
in JS and matching CSS:

  - `FADE_MS` (PublicChatView.tsx): 220ms -> 550ms. The setTimeout
    window before `setCommittedIndex` flips the painted persona.
  - CSS opacity transition (.siteBackground in
    PublicChatView.module.css, .desktopBackground in
    MockAuraApp.module.css): 220ms ease -> 400ms ease-in-out. The
    duration mismatch between the CSS tween (400ms) and the JS
    timer (550ms) is intentional — it leaves the layer pinned at
    opacity 0 for ~150ms after the fade-out tween settles,
    producing a visible "blank hold" between the two halves of
    the swap so the dissolve reads as two distinct gestures
    instead of one uninterrupted 800ms fade.
  - Easing: `ease` -> `ease-in-out`. Slowing both the start AND
    end of the tween exaggerates the perceptual change near
    opacity 1 (where the eye is most sensitive), so the fade
    feels deliberate instead of snappy. Reduced-motion override
    still kills the transition entirely.

Both surfaces tween together because they share the same duration +
easing string, and the JS timer is the only source of truth for the
swap moment — the CSS just paints whatever opacity React publishes.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: style(public-chat): dissolve persona swap through layered overlap
rawCommits.body:
Replaces the previous fade-out -> blank-hold -> fade-in sequence with a true cross-dissolve. The user's feedback was that the ~150ms all-black midpoint felt like a separate "off" state instead of one transition, so the swap now reads as the OLD persona dissolving into the NEW one with no dark moment. How it works: - On click `PublicChatView` advances `committedIndex` to `activeIndex` in the SAME render (no more FADE_MS delay before painting the new persona). At the same time, the PREVIOUS committed persona is captured into an `outgoing` snapshot in state. - The new persona's `.siteBackground` + `MockAuraApp` `.desktopBackground` both mount at full opacity for that paint. A SECOND copy of each (carrying the outgoing snapshot) mounts on top with `.siteBackgroundLeaving` / `.desktopBackgroundLeaving` — keyframe animations that tween the layer's own opacity 1 -> 0 over 550ms. - As the outgoing layer dissolves, the new layer underneath is revealed. The compositing math is clean — `(1 - X) * leaving + X * entering` always sums to a fully-opaque image at every X — because the entering layer never participates in the tween. No parent-bg leak at the midpoint, no choppy seam. - 50ms after the animation completes a setTimeout in `PublicChatView` clears the outgoing snapshot from state, unmounting the second layer. Each layer is still a SINGLE `
` with the persona color on itself and the wallpaper `` as its only child, so color + image inside one persona snapshot always dissolve as one unit (the "wallpaper + image as one div" constraint the user asked for earlier). The layering is purely between the OLD snapshot and the NEW one. State machine uses the "Adjusting State Based on Props" pattern from the React docs — detecting the activeIndex change during render guarantees both layers land in the SAME paint as the click. Deferring the outgoing-layer mount to a useEffect would mean the new layer paints alone for one frame before the outgoing layer mounts on top, which would look like a snap-in. Also drops the now-dead `desktopBackgroundOpacity` prop chain from `ComposePanel` -> `MockAuraApp` since the swap no longer toggles a single element's opacity; replaces it with the `outgoingDesktopBackground` snapshot prop. Co-authored-by: Cursor

rawCommits.subject: feat(marketing): centered /product hero with flow video + shared CTA
rawCommits.body:
Redesigns the public `/product` page's first viewport so the
headline owns the screen and the AURA visual-loop video flows
below it as a continuous scroll-revealed band. Four coordinated
pieces:

1. CreateAgentButton (new shared component)
   - Extracts the neon-glow "Create your agent" CTA pill out of
     `PublicChatView` so the public landing AND the `/product`
     hero mount the same chrome. Styles lifted verbatim from
     the prior `PublicChatView.module.css` `.ctaButton` block
     (same alphas, same blur radii, same shadow stops) so
     landing and product surfaces render identically — only the
     `--glow` hue ever differs (the landing publishes the
     active persona's `siteCtaGlowColor`; the product hero
     leaves it unset and gets the default neon-violet).
   - PublicChatView keeps its inline `<button>` for now; the
     shared component is opt-in via import. Future cleanup can
     swap the landing's inline button to the shared one without
     touching the styles.

2. PageHero (additive prop surface)
   - `centered` boolean: switches the hero to a vertically-
     centered, single-column layout. The headline lands at the
     true 50vh midpoint via a fit-content `.pageHeroCenteredStack`
     wrapper that becomes the parent column's sole flex child,
     so `justify-content: center` math is exact regardless of
     what flows below.
   - `backgroundVideoSrc` / `backgroundImageSrc`: opt-in
     full-bleed media slots. In NON-centered mode they paint as
     absolutely-positioned backdrops behind the content layer
     (z-index 0/1) with a side-only vignette over them — left/
     right thirds nearly solid black, narrow keyhole at center
     so only the brightest part of an orb video pokes through.
     In CENTERED mode the video moves to a flowing block sibling
     of `.pageHeroContent` instead (see below).
   - `headlineCta` ReactNode slot: optional element rendered
     directly beneath the headline. Centered mode renders it
     inside the centered stack between description and CTA;
     non-centered mode renders it inline between headline and
     description. ProductView passes `<CreateAgentButton />`
     here so the landing's CTA pill sits under the centered
     headline.
   - `.pageHeroFlowVideo`: the centered-mode video block. Mounts
     AFTER `.pageHeroContent` and uses `margin-top: calc(viewport
     / -3)` so its top edge anchors at ~2/3 of the viewport on
     load (i.e. a ~33vh peek strip at the bottom of the screen
     invites scroll, with the rest of the loop revealed by
     scrolling down). Top 22% is masked from transparent → black
     so the video materializes smoothly out of the page bg with
     no hard seam where it meets the empty space above it.
   - Type ramp: centered headline scales `clamp(26px, 4.3vw,
     48px)` (0.85x the prior left-aligned ramp) and paints
     `#f7f8fb` against the section's `#000` background. The
     centered description steps down to `#a3a3a8`, opening a
     ~85-unit brightness gap below the near-white headline
     instead of the prior ~30-unit delta between
     `--color-text-primary` and `--color-text-secondary`. Both
     overrides are scoped to the centered-hero descendant
     selectors so the rest of the app's text tokens stay on
     the system defaults.

3. ProductView (consumer)
   - Switches `/product` to use `centered` + `backgroundVideoSrc`
     + `headlineCta` with the new headline "Your Personal
     Agent." (was "The Open Intelligence Network") and the new
     description focused on the secure-VM value prop.
   - New `ProductView.module.css` narrows the column on
     `/product` only by overriding the shared
     `--marketing-content-max-width` custom property from `75%`
     to `63.75%` (~15% narrower than the landing's persona-wall
     column). Uses `display: contents` so the wrapper itself
     adds no layout box — it just publishes the narrower max-
     width to descendants. Other marketing views (Changelog,
     Feedback, Pricing) keep inheriting the global `75%`.
   - Test updates the headline assertion to the new copy.

4. AuraShell (z-index containment)
   - Adds `isolation: isolate` to `.mainPanel`. Without it, the
     new `.pageHeroFlowVideo` at z-index 2 (and any other
     z-indexed content inside the product hero) participates in
     the SAME stacking context as the public sidebar overlay
     (`.sidebar` at z-index 2 in `.body`'s context), and the
     later-in-DOM main-panel content wins the tie — visibly
     hiding the left nav under the `/product` hero video. The
     `isolation` declaration forms a fresh stacking context on
     the main panel so its descendant z-indexes can't escape
     past the sidebar.

Typecheck + lint clean for touched files; marketing + public-chat
tests (16 files, 74 tests) pass.

rawCommits.body:
Updates the explanatory comment on `.pageHeroFlowVideo` to match
the `--shell-chrome-outer-height`-based body math the rest of the
centered-hero block already uses. The CSS itself was unchanged in
the prior commit — only the comment still talked about
"100vh / 33vh" viewport units, while the actual `calc()`
expressions on `.pageHeroContentCentered` (`min-height`) and
`.pageHeroFlowVideo` (`margin-top`) both subtract
`2 * var(--shell-chrome-outer-height, 42px)` to land at the AURA
"body" (the area between the top titlebar pill and the bottom
taskbar pill) rather than the raw viewport.

New comment walks through the same math the existing CSS
implements:
  - Content area: 100vh − 2 × outer-height (~100vh − 84px)
  - Video pulled up: 1/3 of body height
  - Video actual start: ~2/3 down the visible body
  - Peek strip on load: ~1/3 of the body

No CSS rules, selectors, or values change — purely a docstring
sync so the next reader doesn't think the comment math
(viewport-relative) and the calc math (body-relative) disagree.

rawCommits.subject: fix(public-chat): make CTA shimmer actually paint a visible sweep
rawCommits.body:
Three things were keeping the shimmer band invisible:

1. Stops were alpha variations of white over a dark pill. Once they
   composited against the dark fill they read as effectively the same
   shade, so even though the gradient was animating there was no
   perceivable contrast between base and peak. Switched to opaque
   colors (medium gray #8a8a98 base, #ffffff peak) so the highlight
   band reads as a clear moving sheen regardless of how dark or
   blown-out the pill fill happens to be (idle vs hover-bloom).

2. The span was rendering inline. Some engines won't re-paint a
   `background-clip: text` gradient as the `background-position`
   animates on an inline element. Promoting the label to
   `inline-block` and hinting `will-change: background-position`
   forces the gradient onto its own paint layer so the animation
   actually ticks frame-to-frame.

3. CSS Modules was hashing the `@keyframes` name. The intra-file
   `animation` reference is normally rewritten to match, but to
   remove the variable entirely the keyframes are now declared with
   `:global(ctaShimmer)` so the name is guaranteed to resolve at
   runtime no matter what the modules pipeline does.

Also adds a plain `color: transparent` next to
`-webkit-text-fill-color: transparent` so non-WebKit engines that
ignore the prefixed property still let the gradient show through.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(public-chat): drop :global(...) wrapper that froze the CTA shimmer
rawCommits.body:
Last round wrapped the keyframes as `@keyframes :global(ctaShimmer)`
on the theory it would guarantee the `animation` reference resolved
through Vite's CSS Modules pipeline. The opposite happened - the
`@keyframes :global(name)` form isn't a standard CSS Modules
construct, so the keyframes never registered while the in-file
`animation: ctaShimmer ...` reference was still re-written to the
scoped name. Net effect: the gradient was painted but the animation
never ticked, leaving the label frozen at the 0% keyframe (which
parks the #ffffff peak off the right edge and shows only the
#8a8a98 base - exactly the flat-gray render in the latest
screenshot).

Every other @keyframes in the codebase (`mockAuraDesktopBgFadeOut`,
`dmWindowExpand`, `typewriterCaretBlink`, `spinRing`, ...) just
declares as plain `@keyframes name { ... }` inside its module and
animates fine, because Vite's CSS Modules pipeline transparently
rewrites the in-file `animation` shorthand to match the scoped
keyframes name. Match that convention - the sweep ticks again and
the bright white band sweeps across the label every 2.6s as
intended.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: tune(public-chat): snappier active-pill slide + always-on transition
rawCommits.body:
Two paired tweaks to the public sidebar footer's sliding active
pill in `PublicSidebarFooter.module.css`:

1. Drop the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` guard that
   was silently flipping the slide into a hard jump on OSes with
   reduced-motion enabled at the system level (e.g. Windows' "Show
   animations" off). The slide is a load-bearing navigation
   affordance — it's the only visual that ties the previously-
   active row to the newly-clicked one ("the pill came FROM
   there") — so suppressing it left motion-sensitive visitors
   seeing a re-paint-style jump rather than a respectful no-motion
   fallback. The CTA shimmer in PublicChatView still honors
   reduced-motion because its motion is purely decorative (a glow
   loop), not a navigation cue, so the precedents diverge on
   purpose.

2. Speed the transform transition from 0.25s -> 0.15s and pull
   height + opacity to the same 0.15s beat so the mount fade-in
   resolves on the same tick as a slide arrival. Per direct user
   feedback the prior 0.25s read as draggy on quick successive
   clicks between adjacent rows because the slide hadn't finished
   settling before the next click started a new one; 0.15s is
   short enough to keep up with fast nav traversal while staying
   long enough to register the click-to-pill continuity.

rawCommits.subject: test(harness): invariant tests pin retry_action + classification contract
rawCommits.body:
Pins the cross-cutting invariants Phase 6's retry-policy commit
(6cd7181) did not pin individually so future strips cannot silently
break the aura-harness <-> aura-os retry handshake:

- is_retryable() and retry_action(0) != Terminal stay consistent for
  every HarnessFailureKind variant AND every attempt 0..=5
  (is_retryable_matches_retry_action_for_every_kind_and_attempt).
  Independent ladder-monotonicity invariant: a kind whose attempt-0
  action is Terminal stays Terminal at every higher attempt — a
  future kind that "un-terminals" at attempt N would let the
  reconciler resurrect tasks legacy callers think are permanently
  failed.
- RetryAction serializes as the EXACT snake_case strings 'retry',
  'retry_with_decomposition', 'terminal' on the wire AND
  round-trips through serde_json — pins the on-wire format
  aura-harness's task_decomposed event consumers (Phase 5) and the
  task_retrying event payload emitter (Phase 6's
  emit_task_retrying_signal) pattern-match against
  (retry_action_serializes_to_snake_case_strings).
- The literal aura-harness verdict 'task completed without any file
  operations — completion not verified' (em dash U+2014, byte-for-
  byte) classifies as ResearchLoopAbort AND escalates Retry ->
  RetryWithDecomposition -> Terminal across attempts 0/1/2
  (verbatim_validate_execution_message_classifies_as_research_loop_abort).
  Pairs with the aura-harness invariant test
  (validate_execution_emits_verbatim_research_loop_abort_message)
  which pins the emitter side; together they guard the cross-repo
  string contract on both ends.

SKIPPED — production code is not directly testable in isolation:
- 'research_loop_abort_attempt_2_results_in_terminal_no_retry_
  scheduled' and 'research_loop_abort_attempt_1_emits_retry_with_
  decomposition_in_payload' from the plan: the per-attempt retry
  decision lives in maybe_apply_task_level_retry inside
  apps/aura-os-server/src/handlers/dev_loop/streaming/side_effects/
  retry.rs, which is module-private and tightly coupled to the
  storage client. Driving it end-to-end from a black-box test
  would require either widening visibility or building a
  storage-client mock substantially larger than the assertion it
  enables. The contract those tests would pin is fully covered at
  the type level by the new attempt-aware

  invariant + Phase 6's
  research_loop_abort_escalates_through_decomposition (already in
  signals/mod.rs) which together pin the exact ladder
  Retry@0 -> RetryWithDecomposition@1 -> Terminal@2 the reconciler

rawCommits.subject: feat(tasks): add Re-do button for completed tasks
rawCommits.body:
Adds a user-initiated "Re-do" path that lets a user re-run a task
already in `done`. Mirrors the failed-Retry pattern: reset to
`ready` then immediately fire a one-shot harness run.

Backend
- Open the `done -> ready` edge in the bridge planner
  (`crates/aura-os-tasks/src/transition.rs`) and the server-side
  `validate_transition` (`task_service.rs`). Done remains terminal
  for every other target so the auto-retry ladder cannot resurrect
  completed tasks on its own.
- Add `redo_task` handler at
  `POST /api/projects/:project_id/tasks/:task_id/redo`. Drives
  `safe_transition(.., Ready)` and clears the persisted `attempts`
  counter so the user-initiated re-do gets a fresh
  `MAX_TASK_ATTEMPTS` budget (failure-Retry intentionally preserves
  it).
- Document the matching aura-network validator change in
  `docs/migrations/2026-05-25-task-redo-transition.md`.

Frontend
- Add `redoTask` to the API client and a `handleRedo` callback
  alongside `handleRetry` in `useTaskPreviewData`.
- Render a `RefreshCw` Re-do button in `TaskMetaSection`, shown
  only when `effectiveStatus === "done"` (next to where Retry
  appears for failed tasks).

Tests
- Bridge planner: replace `done_is_terminal` with
  `done_can_only_become_ready` plus a single-hop assertion.
- API: `redo_resets_done_task_to_ready_and_clears_attempts` and
  `redo_unknown_task_returns_not_found`.
- FE: `redoTask` URL test and a TaskPreview test that asserts
  clicking Re-do drives `redoTask` then `runTask`.

rawCommits.subject: fix(thinking): close earlier thinking blocks during multi-segment turns
rawCommits.body:
`ActivityTimeline` used to forward the turn-level `isStreaming` flag
to every `ThinkingBlock`, so during a `thinking -> tool -> thinking`
turn every block rendered as "Thinking..." with the shimmer and
stayed force-expanded even though `closeCurrentThinkingSegment` had
already stamped `durationMs` on the earlier segments. `Block` also
only handled the `false -> true` edge of `forceExpanded`, so once the
streaming bubble released the force-expand on the just-closed
segment the body stayed open from the streaming-era state.

Derive a per-segment `isStreaming = isStreaming && item.durationMs == null`
in `ActivityTimeline` and collapse `Block` back to `defaultExpanded`
on the `forceExpanded` falling edge (ref-guarded so a steady-state
`defaultExpanded` change doesn't clobber a user's manual toggle on
non-forced blocks). Result: only the trailing live segment shows
"Thinking..."; earlier ones flip to "Thought for X" and collapse.

rawCommits.subject: fix(scrollbar): stop OverlayScrollbar flicker when hovering the thumb
rawCommits.body:
After 5ca81fdb5 widened the thumb hit area to 12px and toggled its
pointer-events based on .scrollThumbVisible, hovering the thumb caused
a feedback loop: the thumb is a sibling (not descendant) of the scroll
container, so moving the cursor onto it fired mouseleave on the
container -> hovered=false -> thumb faded and pointer-events: none ->
cursor fell back to the container -> mouseenter -> hovered=true ->
repeat, flickering the thumb opacity indefinitely.

Track mouseenter/mouseleave on containerRef.current.parentElement
(fallback to the container) so hover is detected on the wrapper that
holds both the scroll container and the scroll track. The thumb is a
descendant of that wrapper in every call site (LeftMenuTree, AgentList,
FeedbackList, SettingsView, TaskOutputPanel, OrgSettingsPanel, etc.),
so the cursor moving onto it no longer leaves the hover region.

Includes a regression test that simulates the cursor crossing from the
scroll container onto a sibling thumb and asserts visibility stays
true.

rawCommits.subject: sidekick(task-head): hydrate per-task context pill for cold-loaded rows
rawCommits.body:
Previously the per-task context-usage pill only appeared while a task
was actively streaming (or had streamed during this browser session).
After a page reload — or whenever the user opened the Task Preview for
a task that finished in a prior session — the pill stayed hidden
because `useContextUsageStore` had no entry for `taskStreamKey(taskId)`.

Adds a task-scoped REST endpoint and wires it through the widget so
historical task rows hydrate from storage on mount.

Backend:
- `GET /api/projects/:project_id/tasks/:task_id/context-usage` returns
  the latest persisted `assistant_message_end.usage.context_*` payload
  whose `content.task_id` matches the requested task. Resolves the
  storage session id via the in-memory `task_output_cache` first, then
  falls back to `storage.get_task(...)` so cold reads still work. New
  `apps/aura-os-server/src/handlers/tasks/context_usage.rs` module
  mirrors the parsing in
  `handlers/agents/sessions::latest_context_usage_for_session` but
  filters by `task_id` so a session that ran multiple tasks doesn't
  return another task's last turn. Reuses the existing
  `ContextUsageResponse` shape; promoted the `sessions` module to
  `pub(crate)` so the type and helpers are reachable from `tasks/`.

Frontend:
- `tasksApi.getContextUsage(projectId, taskId)` client.
- `TaskHeaderContextUsage` now accepts `projectId` and calls
  `useHydrateContextUtilization(taskStreamKey, fetcher, taskId)` so
  the store is seeded on mount. The hook's existing guards (skip when
  resetting, when streaming, or when a value already exists) prevent
  the fetch from clobbering fresher live data.
- `ActiveTaskStream`, `CompletedTaskOutput`, and `Preview` pass the
  project id (from `useProjectActions`, a prop, and `task.project_id`
  respectively) so all three surfaces hydrate consistently.

Tests:
- `CompletedTaskOutput.test.tsx` and `TaskPreview.test.tsx` mock
  `hooks/stream/hooks`; extended their mocks to include `useIsStreaming`
  (and a few siblings) now that `TaskHeaderContextUsage` transitively
  pulls them in via the hydration hook.

Vitest delta vs main: 0 new failures (30 → 30, +1 passing).
