rawCommits.subject: fix(agents): persist sentinel to silence permissions heal storm across restarts
rawCommits.body:
The aura-network upstream silently drops the `permissions` column on
both GET and PUT round-trips. The existing safety net adopts the
local shadow, attempts a one-shot heal PUT, and dedupes per process
-- but every boot still emits ~22 WARNs (one GET-side + one PUT-side
per agent) because the dedup never survived a restart.

Persist a `permissions:upstream_drops_column` settings key the first
time a heal PUT confirms upstream drops the column on writes. When
the sentinel is set, `reconcile_permissions_with_shadow` keeps
adopting the shadow (the contract is unchanged) but skips the
per-agent WARN and the doomed PUT entirely, emitting a single
boot-time INFO instead. The sentinel auto-clears the moment upstream
returns a non-empty bundle, so a fixed deployment self-heals without
any manual reset.

After the next boot persists the sentinel, subsequent boots drop
from ~22 WARNs to zero (one INFO line).

Three new tests pin the new contract:
- `reconcile_with_sentinel_set_still_adopts_shadow` -- safety net
  unchanged when sentinel is set
- `reconcile_clears_sentinel_when_upstream_returns_non_empty` --
  auto-clear path
- `sentinel_survives_across_service_instances` -- cross-process
  persistence via the underlying SettingsStore

rawCommits.subject: fix(dev-loop): stop swallowing harness 409 wedge and unblock Play
rawCommits.body:
Clicking Play could leave the AutomationBar looking idle even after the
server returned 409 ("a dev loop is already running") for a stale
harness automaton inherited across an aura-os-server restart. Three
things conspired:

1. The harness's 409 body shape varied between builds. The legacy
   parser only matched the free-text `automaton_id: ` substring, so
   structured `{"automaton_id": ...}` bodies fell through as
   `Conflict(None)` and the adopt-or-stop-and-restart path in
   `start_or_adopt` was bypassed.
2. The server then mapped that bare conflict to an opaque 409 with no
   machine-readable code, so the UI could not distinguish the wedge
   from a generic failure.
3. `useAutomationStatus.handleStart` caught the error and only logged
   to `console.error`, leaving the Play button clickable and offering
   no path to recovery.

Hardens the parser (`extract_conflict_automaton_id`) to accept
top-level / nested `data.*` / legacy-substring shapes so the adopt
branch can recover on every harness build. Adds
`ApiError::automation_already_running` (machine-readable code +
`data.automaton_id`) for the truly opaque case, and wires the
AutomationBar to render a "Reset and retry" ModalConfirm that calls
`stopLoop` then `startLoop` in one click. Generic Start failures now
surface as a "Start failed" Dismiss modal instead of disappearing into
the console.

Pinned by 8 new parser unit tests plus 2 AutomationBar UI tests.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(automation-bar): scope loop-terminal events to the bound Loop
rawCommits.body:
Every forwarder teardown — including the ephemeral task-runner
automatons that `run_single_task` mints per task — emits
`loop_finished`. The AutomationBar's `useAutomationStatus` hook
filtered those events by `project_id` only, so an ephemeral runner's
natural end (or a transient WS close on the main forwarder that
arrives with the same `agent_id` as the bound Loop on the next start)
would dispatch `loopFinished` to the reducer, `filterAgent` would
clear the bound id from the agents list, and the StatusBadge would
flip back to "idle" — even while the harness automaton kept turning
out DevLoopBootstrap turns.

Tighten the WS subscriptions for `LoopStopped` / `LoopFinished` /
`LoopPaused` / `LoopResumed` to also require `event.agent_id ===
boundLoopId` once the bound Loop is known. `LoopStarted` still uses
the project-only filter so it can populate the binding from the first
WS frame on a fresh project; `TaskStarted` likewise stays project-
only because ephemeral runners are the canonical preparing→active
promotion signal. Apply the same scoping to the project-level
`useLoopActive` hook so per-task `RunTaskButton`s don't flicker their
"ready" affordance back on while the dev loop is still running.

Includes `use-loop-active.test.ts` regression coverage for the
ephemeral-vs-bound discrimination and the project-only fallback when
no bound Loop id has been hydrated yet.

rawCommits.subject: fix(harness-client): give /automaton/start a 60s per-call budget
rawCommits.body:
The harness's `bridge.start_dev_loop_with_capabilities` /
`run_task_with_capabilities` does identity, tool, skill, and system-
prompt resolution BEFORE it returns the automaton id, and on a
freshly-launched harness or a project with a large tool catalog that
work can comfortably exceed `AutomatonClient`'s client-wide 12s
`timeout(...)` default. When it does, the harness happily keeps
building the automaton (and starts firing turns visible in its own
log), but the os-server's POST has already given up with
`reqwest::Error { is_timeout: true }` — which `start_or_adopt::
map_start_error` folds into a 503 `service_unavailable`, the
AutomationBar shows "Start failed", and a now-orphan automaton runs
on the harness with no FE control surface.

Add a per-call `.timeout(60s)` override on `AutomatonClient::start()`
so a slow harness cold-start no longer trips the global budget.
Connect / DNS failures still surface fast via the unchanged
`connect_timeout(3s)`, so a genuinely-unreachable harness still
fails quickly — the only thing this extra budget changes is "harness
is alive and busy setting up" vs "harness is unreachable".

Leaves the other endpoints (pause / stop / status / resume /
resolve_workspace) on the original 12s default since they are
naturally short-running.

rawCommits.subject: fix: surface model errors early, dedupe auth sync, simplify task transitions
rawCommits.body:
Three independent fixes that were sitting together in the working tree.

1. Run-task model resolution
   Run buttons used to send `null` when the chat-UI store hadn't hydrated
   `selectedModel` for the agent, which made the harness pick a stale
   default and surfaced as a misleading 502 from the start endpoint.
   - `RunTaskButton.tsx` and `useTaskPreviewData.ts` now resolve a model
     id via `loadPersistedModel("default", undefined, agentInstanceId)`
     before calling `api.runTask`, so the payload is always a non-empty
     string.
   - `automation-loop-store.ts`'s `useAutomationModel` falls back to the
     last main-LLM (`aura_harness`) chat pick when the per-project slot
     is empty, matching the documented (per-project) -> (global chat) ->
     (adapter default) chain.
   - `AutomationModelPicker.tsx` consumes the effective id from the
     store instead of recomputing the fallback inline.
   - `dev_loop/start/mod.rs::require_model` returns a `400 Bad Request`
     with a clear message when the picked model is missing or empty,
     instead of forwarding to the harness and returning a generic 502.
   - `dev_loop/start/start_or_adopt.rs` warn-logs the harness response
     body on 5xx so future regressions are diagnosable from logs alone.
   - Tests in `TaskPreview.test.tsx` assert on `expect.any(String)` for
     the model arg now that the fallback always yields a non-empty id.

2. Per-token aura-network sync dedupe
   The frontend host probe polls `GET /api/auth/session` every 20s purely
   for connectivity; `sync_user_to_network` was firing a fresh
   aura-network round-trip and a session-store write on every one of
   those polls. Adds a 5-minute per-token dedupe via a static
   `DashMap<access_token, Instant>` (`LAST_NETWORK_SYNC`):
   - `sync_user_to_network` takes a new `force: bool`. All callers pass
     `false` except `POST /api/auth/validate`, which is the explicit
     refresh contract and must bypass the cache.
   - `logout` calls a new `clear_user_network_sync_dedupe(jwt)` so we
     don't retain entries for invalidated tokens.

3. Task transition handler refactor
   `transition_task` now delegates to `aura_os_tasks::safe_transition`
   instead of open-coding the fetch/validate/transition/refetch dance.
   The handler keeps the same external behaviour (404 stays 404, illegal
   transitions stay 400 with a readable message, storage 400s pass
   through) but the body shrinks from ~40 lines to ~15.

Verified: `cargo check -p aura-os-server`, dev_loop::start unit tests
(6 passed), and `vitest run` over AutomationBar / TaskPreview /
RunTaskButton / automation-loop-store (105 tests passed).

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

final lifecycle transition invisible next to the file ops and

Also broadcast a new `task_updated` event from every task CRUD/

rawCommits.subject: fix(dev-loop): re-emit LoopOpened on adopt-shortcut so FE spinners light up
rawCommits.body:
The adopt-shortcut path in `dev_loop/run/mod.rs::adopt_shortcut_outcome`
reuses the existing automaton forwarder and therefore skips
`register_active_automaton` (the cold-path entry point that calls
`LoopRegistry::open` and mints the only `LoopOpened` event the
`loop_events_bridge` mirrors to the FE). The legacy `loop_started`
event was already re-emitted on the WS broadcast, which keeps the
HTTP-driven `AutomationBar` happy, but the three live surfaces that
read from `useLoopActivityStore` (sidekick nav-bar loop ring, per-task
spinner in `TaskList`, Run pane via `useLoopActive`) only ingest the
typed `loop_opened` / `loop_activity_changed` frames produced by
`aura-os-events`'s `EventHub`. Without a re-published `LoopOpened`
those selectors (see `interface/src/stores/loop-activity-store.ts`)
see an empty `loops` map for the entire reused-loop lifetime and the
spinners stay dark even while the harness is working.

Adds `LoopRegistry::re_emit_loop_opened(&LoopId) -> bool`, a non-
allocating re-publish that snapshots the current `LoopActivity` and
fires a fresh `DomainEvent::LoopOpened` for an already-open slot
(no-op if absent). Wired into `adopt_shortcut_outcome` after the
existing `emit_domain_event("loop_started", ...)`. The new event
flows through `loop_events_bridge` and reaches the FE as a
`loop_opened` WS frame, seeding `useLoopActivityStore.loops` so the
downstream selectors (`selectTaskActivity`, the nav-ring aggregator)
have something to bind to. A `tracing::debug!` log line covers the
genuinely-missing-slot case so a future regression there is findable
without paying log volume in healthy runs.

Unit tests in `crates/aura-os-loops/src/registry/tests.rs` cover the
happy path (re-emit publishes a `LoopOpened` carrying the current
activity snapshot) and the no-op path (unknown loop id does not
publish).

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(task-stream): isolate synthetic transition emits from lifecycle handlers
rawCommits.body:
`handleTaskStarted` / `handleTaskCompleted` / `handleTaskFailed` in
`interface/src/stores/task-stream-bootstrap.ts` call
`emitSyntheticTransitionBlock` to inject a decorative
`ready -> in_progress` / `in_progress -> done` / `in_progress -> failed`
card into the activity timeline. The synthetic emit drives the same
`handleToolCallStarted` + `handleToolCallSnapshot` + `handleToolResult`
reducer chain a real tool call would, which means a malformed
stream-entry refs bag (e.g. the event arrives before any chat-side
hook had a chance to initialise its refs) can throw inside the
reducer and prevent the rest of the handler from running.

For `handleTaskCompleted` and `handleTaskFailed` this matters: the
synthetic emit sits BEFORE `finalizeStream`, `completeTask` /
`failTask`, `setLiveStatus("done")` / `setLiveStatus("failed")`, and
`snapshotTaskTurns`. A throw inside the synthetic chain would leave
the Run panel row stuck on "active" forever and never persist the
final assistant turn — exactly the "AutomationBar says working but
Run pane is empty" shape the live-updates regression presents.

Wraps each of the three call sites in a small try/catch that logs a
`console.warn` in DEV only, leaving the lifecycle work
(`addTask`, `setLiveStatus`, `completeTask`, `failTask`,
`snapshotTaskTurns`) reachable even if the decorative card emit
fails. Adds two unit tests in
`interface/src/stores/task-stream-bootstrap.test.ts` that mock
`handleToolCallStarted` to throw once and assert the panel row still
appears on `TaskStarted` and transitions to "completed" on
`TaskCompleted`.

rawCommits.subject: fix(task-output): persist + render full run history across reloads
rawCommits.body:
Bug: after a build run completed or failed, the Run pane and Tasks
preview collapsed the row to "No output captured for this run." even
when the dev loop had streamed text, tool cards, and verification
steps. The same symptom hit three orthogonal entry paths -- live
finalize, page reload, and background runs the current UI never
streamed -- because the rehydrate chain dropped or never fetched the
structured artifacts.

Fixes:

- Panel-store: PanelTaskEntry now carries `sessionId` (plus
  `agentInstanceId` round-tripping). `addTask` / `hydrateActiveTask`
  / `reconcileStatuses` populate the field from the live
  `TaskStarted` event and from the persisted `tasks.session_id`
  column at reload, so the rehydrate path always knows which
  session to replay. A re-run replaces a stale `sessionId` so the
  pane doesn't show the previous attempt's transcript.
- Shared step mapping: `mapBuildSteps` / `mapTestSteps` /
  `mapGitSteps` are hoisted out of `use-task-output-hydration.ts`
  into `hooks/task-step-mapping.ts`. The Tasks-tab hook and the
  Run-pane `useTaskOutputView` now share one normaliser instead of
  diverging (the Run pane previously dropped the steps entirely).
- View parity: `useTaskOutputView` calls `api.getTaskOutput` and
  forwards build/test/git steps to `seedTaskOutput`, matching the
  Tasks-tab hydration. A new effect falls back to
  `api.listSessionEvents` (single-flighted through the existing
  hydration cache) when the local `task-turn-cache` is empty and
  the entry has a `sessionId` + `agentInstanceId`, normalising the
  wire payload through `buildDisplayEvents` and mirroring it into
  the turn cache so siblings skip the round trip.
- Body fallback: `CompletedTaskOutput` renders the structured
  build/test/git steps via `VerificationStepItem` / `GitStepItem`
  whenever the row has no chat events or text. Suppressed in the
  Tasks-tab `TaskPreview` (which already shows dedicated
  verification sections above) via a new `showStepsFallback` prop.

Tests:

- task-output-panel-store: addTask/refresh-on-rerun stores
  sessionId; reconcileStatuses backfills sessionId /
  agentInstanceId without clobbering live values, and seeds them
  on cold-boot rows.
- task-stream-bootstrap: TaskStarted propagates session_id /
  agent_id onto the panel entry; re-run replaces a stale sessionId.
- CompletedTaskOutput: renders build / test / git step rows from
  the fallback when no events/text are present, and honours
  `showStepsFallback={false}` for embeddings that render their own
  verification sections.

was masking the placeholder for the entire active window.

text/tool delta. Synthetic transition cards still render in the

Plan todo: backend half of regression-tests.

The dev-loop `adopt_shortcut_outcome` calls
`LoopRegistry::re_emit_loop_opened(&loop_id)` so the bridge mirrors a
fresh `{"type":"loop_opened",...}` JSON frame onto `event_broadcast`
each time a forwarder is reused. Without that re-emit, the FE's
`useLoopActivityStore` stays empty for the entire lifetime of a
reused loop and the three live surfaces that depend on it (nav-bar
loop ring, per-task row spinners, Run pane) sit idle even while the
harness is actively working.

The registry helper already has unit tests in `aura-os-loops`
(`registry::tests::re_emit_loop_opened_publishes_for_known_loop` and
`...is_noop_for_unknown_loop`), but nothing was pinning the
end-to-end wire-shape contract: that the typed `LoopOpened` lands as
a JSON frame on `event_broadcast` with the `loop_id` / `activity` /
`project_id` / `agent_instance_id` fields the FE's
`useLoopActivityStore` selectors key off.

Add two integration tests under
`tests/api_tests/loop_adopt_shortcut.rs`:

1. Happy path — open a loop, drain the inaugural `loop_opened`,
   call `re_emit_loop_opened`, assert a SECOND `loop_opened` JSON
   frame lands with `activity.status` as a string (snake_case
   `LoopStatus` serialisation pinned).
2. Missing-slot — call `re_emit_loop_opened` on an unknown
   `loop_id`, assert it returns `false` and nothing lands on
   `event_broadcast` (matches the `tracing::debug!` no-op path in
   `adopt_shortcut_outcome`).

The bare `build_test_app` harness skips the production
`spawn_loop_events_bridge` wiring (that lives in `app_builder`), so
the test stands the bridge up by hand against the same `event_hub` /
`event_broadcast` the test app already holds. The bridge spawner
was promoted from `pub(crate)` to `pub` (landed inside the
sibling `775297c92` commit) so integration tests can mount it
directly rather than duplicating the JSON render logic.

Tested with `cargo test -p aura-os-server --test api_tests` —
26 passed including the two new cases. The pre-existing
Windows-only `agent_update_ceo_test.exe` integration binary still
fails to launch with os error 740 (elevation) — unrelated, see the
plan's "Pre-existing breakage to tolerate" note.

A redundant `task_completed` / `task_failed` for the same task hit
`persist_task_output` after the cache entry had been removed by the
first persist. A trailing `token_usage` event (emitted right after

rawCommits.subject: feat(dev_loop): emit automation lifecycle + per-event tracing under aura::automation
rawCommits.body:
Mirror the dev-loop streaming pipeline's harness-event flow onto a
dedicated `aura::automation` tracing target so `aura-os-desktop`'s
stderr console (and the rolling desktop.log) actually surface what an
automation run is doing.

Before this change, the only automation-related line a console
operator saw was `tower_http`'s `POST /api/projects/.../loop/start`
trace and the rare failure-path `warn!`. Lifecycle and per-event
signals lived only inside `emit_log_line` / `emit_domain_event` --
i.e. they reached the frontend's SidekickLog but never `tracing`,
leaving the console blind once the loop was running.

New emissions, all targeted at `aura::automation`:

- `register.rs`: `automation run registered` (info) for both
  `register_automation` and `register_single_task`, with mode,
  automaton_id, adopted, and session_id.
- `forwarder.rs`: `forwarder listening for harness events` on
  startup (info), `automation loop finished` with outcome + reason
  on teardown (info), `harness event` per raw event (debug) with
  event_type + task_id + comma-joined top-level keys, and
  `automation tool call started` (info) for the tool_use_start /
  tool_call_started family (which has no side-effects arm and was
  previously invisible at the info level).
- New helpers `top_level_keys` and `event_tool_name` with unit
  tests; both bounded so a pathologically wide harness payload
  cannot blow up a log line.

Default `EnvFilter` in both `aura-os-desktop` and `aura-os-server`
now pins `aura::automation=info` so the lifecycle is visible out of
the box. `RUST_LOG=aura::automation=debug` opts into the per-event
firehose without flipping the rest of the server into debug.

The companion `side_effects/dispatch.rs` lifecycle info! lines for
task_started / task_completed / task_failed / tool_call_completed /
git_lifecycle were already picked up by 1ca4a190e; this commit
finishes the pipeline.

rawCommits.subject: feat(planning): require structured spec + task content contracts
rawCommits.body:
Tasks extracted from specs were vague because nothing told the LLM what
a good task description should contain - only what to avoid. Specs in
plan mode also only required a `## Definition of Done`, so even a
careful extraction pass had no concrete files, signatures, or
acceptance signals to copy down.

Define and enforce two parallel content contracts:

- Specs must include `## Background / Context`, `## Goals`,
  `## Non-Goals`, `## Affected Files & Modules` (real repo paths),
  `## Interfaces & Signatures` (current and proposed shape pasted
  verbatim from source), `## Design / Approach`,
  `## External References`, and `## Definition of Done`.
- Tasks must include `## Goal`, `## Context` (quoting 1-3 lines from
  the parent spec verbatim), `## Files & Symbols` (real paths plus
  function/type/test names), `## Approach`, `## Acceptance Criteria`,
  and `## Verification` (commands pulled from the spec's
  Definition of Done).

Wire the contracts into every entry point:

- `plan_mode.rs`: add the spec + task contracts to the system-prompt
  suffix and the per-turn user preamble so chat plan mode and the
  dedicated /specs/generate* endpoints stay in lock-step.
- `tasks/extraction.rs`: rewrite `task_extraction_prompt` to require
  the structured task template, demand inspection of the repo before
  writing tasks, forbid invented paths, and point Verification at the
  spec's Definition of Done.
- `specs/gen.rs`: tighten the spec_gen_instruction user message so the
  benchmark/CLI entry point names the structured spec sections too.
- `agent_bootstrap.rs`: extend the CEO SuperAgent rules so non-plan-
  mode chat writes specs and tasks in the same shape.
- `project-control-plane-tools.json`: surface the contracts at the
  tool-schema boundary (create_spec, update_spec, create_task,
  update_task) so the model sees the required headings even outside
  plan mode.
- `task_decompose.rs`: extract the skeleton/fill description templates
  into pure helpers and add an inheritance reminder so auto-decomposed
  child tasks don't lose the parent's `## Files & Symbols`,
  `## Acceptance Criteria`, and `## Verification` sections.

Pin every required heading with regression tests in plan_mode,
extraction, agent_bootstrap, and task_decompose so a drift in any one
prompt is loud rather than silent.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: feat(public-chat): route assistant bubbles through standard LLMOutput
rawCommits.body:
Public chat (desktop + mobile) now renders assistant turns through a
shared PublicChatBubble component backed by LLMOutput, matching every
other LLM surface in the app. The previous inline plain-text bubble
bypassed ActivityTimeline entirely, so the standard collapsible Block
chrome (text segments, code blocks, markdown) never reached public
chat. User messages keep their plain-text rendering; assistant code
and plan messages now flow through LLMOutput; media (image / video /
model3d) variants keep the existing placeholder string since wiring
them through the standard content-block strips is a separate change.

The in-flight assistant turn detection threads `isStreaming=true` to
LLMOutput so the live-streaming chrome engages on the message being
appended by `streamPublicChat`, while every committed prior turn
renders as a terminal Block.

Deviation from the audit's literal recommendation: this change uses
LLMOutput directly rather than the standard MessageBubble /
StreamingBubble envelope (the audit Section E lists both options).
The MessageBubble path presumes an authenticated session — it pulls
in the gallery provider, agent-store cross-agent attribution badge,
ReportBug button, and stream-store entries keyed by agent / session
id — none of which exist on the logged-out public surface. Routing
through LLMOutput delivers the Block chrome (ActivityTimeline,
ReactMarkdown, code highlighting) without dragging the rest of the
authenticated chat infrastructure into the marketing path.

Note: the public-chat backend SSE protocol emits only `text_delta` /
`limit` / `error` frames today (see api/public-chat.ts), so the
Phase 1 synthetic Brain "Thinking..." Block in ActivityTimeline does
not surface in public chat — its `hasAnyTool` gate is always false
here. Real thinking-block surfacing requires the public-chat backend
to forward `thinking_delta` events; a TODO(thinking) marker in
public-chat-store.ts documents the seams that would need to change.

model emits zero `thinking_delta` events but does call tools had no

streaming flag stayed true and it remained force-expanded with a
shimmering "Thinking..." label for the entire turn. During plan-mode
spec creation that left a stale, uncollapsible block at the top of the
chat while specs were created below it. The synthetic placeholder now

rawCommits.subject: fix(activity-timeline): collapse adjacent block borders on row wrappers
rawCommits.body:
The virtualization refactor wrapped each timeline item in its own
`<div>` so `@tanstack/react-virtual` can window the list, which silently
broke `.block + .block { margin-top: -1px }` in Block.module.css — every
Block is now nested inside a row wrapper and is never a true adjacent
sibling of another Block, so the rule stopped matching. Result: a
visible 4-12px gap and a doubled 1px border between every block on
every surface (chat, run pane, task preview).

Move the stacking responsibility up to the row wrappers in
ActivityTimeline.module.css, where the actual DOM siblings now live:

- Drop the dead `.block { margin-top: 4px }` and `.block + .block`
  rules from the Block primitive; spacing is no longer its job.
- Replace `.timeline { gap: 8px }` with `* + *` margin rules so a
  negative margin inside a tool run can actually cancel the spacing
  (flex `gap` cannot be negated).
- For `data-tool-position` mid/last rows apply `margin-top: -1px` to
  pull the row up so its top border lands on the predecessor's bottom
  border. Works for both variants: in the plain timeline it overrides
  the 8px sibling spacing; in the virtual variant it shifts the
  absolutely-positioned row without changing `getBoundingClientRect()`
  dimensions, so the virtualizer's accumulated-size math stays correct.
- For first/mid rows drop `padding-bottom` so the next tool sits flush
  against the predecessor in the virtual variant.

rawCommits.subject: fix(image-gen): deliver SSE completion frame before awaiting persistence
rawCommits.body:
`run_image_upstream_task` was awaiting `persist_completion` BEFORE
sending the terminal `generation_completed` SSE frame. A slow or
unreachable storage backend (locally reproducible) held the inner
loop indefinitely, so the client received heartbeats then nothing
-- cooking pill ran forever and no image ever appeared. Heartbeats
also stopped because we were stuck inside the inner `while let`
loop rather than the outer `timeout(...)`. Reorder so the SSE
frame goes out first and persistence is awaited after (still
best-effort, still attempted on late client disconnect).

Adds `generation_completed_arrives_even_when_storage_hangs` as a
regression gate: drives `run_image_upstream_task` against a router
that emits `completed` immediately and a storage listener that
accepts the persist POST and never replies, asserting the
`generation_completed` frame still reaches the SSE channel within
2s.

rawCommits.subject: fix(activity-timeline): extend border collapse to any adjacent Block rows
rawCommits.body:
The `data-tool-position` collapse introduced in 06d6c6ae1 only fired for
tool <-> tool runs, so a `ThinkingBlock` followed by a tool block (or the
reverse) still rendered an 8-12px gap and a doubled 1px border. Both
are `Block` primitives with the same border, and the screenshot scrap
showed those Block-on-Block boundaries as the visible doubled line.

Generalize the row attribute from "is a tool" to "renders a bordered
Block":

- Stamp `data-block-row="true"` on rows whose rendered node is a Block
  primitive (today `kind === "tool" || kind === "thinking"`). Text rows
  render bare markdown with no border so they intentionally stay off
  the attribute and keep their 12px breathing-room margin.
- Replace the `data-tool-position`-keyed collapse rules with
  `data-block-row` equivalents. `:has(+ [data-block-row])` on the
  predecessor zeroes `padding-bottom` so the virtualized variant's
  accumulated translateY math stays correct; `+ [data-block-row]`
  pulls the successor up 1px to overlap the divider. Both rules fire
  for any cross-kind pair of bordered rows, not just tool <-> tool.
- Drop the thinking <-> tool half of the cross-kind 12px margin rule
  since those pairs now flush-stack. Keep text <-> tool / text <-> thinking
  so prose still has breathing room from bordered blocks.

Tests assert thinking + tool + thinking all carry `data-block-row`
while a text row does not.

rawCommits.subject: fix(sidekick): stabilize task preview live stream and persist prior turns
rawCommits.body:
Removes the visual jank and disappearing blocks reported in the task
preview overlay and Run pane during live streaming.

- ActiveTaskStream renders prior assistant turns from `useStreamEvents`
  as MessageBubbles above the live stream, so blocks no longer vanish at
  every `assistant_message_end` (which wipes the live timeline by design).
- buildDisplayedTimeline drops the `textPending` suppression of tool and
  thinking rows. Tools and thinking now appear in real stream order;
  text segments still reveal character-by-character. Eliminates both the
  pop-in and the mid-stream blink-out previously triggered when a new
  text_delta extended the buffer past the reveal cursor.
- ActivityTimeline only engages the virtualizer when not streaming or
  when the row count crosses 60. Live streams render through a plain
  flex layout, so measureElement no longer shifts every row below as
  block heights settle.
- Synthetic Brain "Thinking..." placeholder renders as a stable sibling
  above the timeline rather than being unshifted into the row list, so
  removing it never reflows surrounding rows.
- useScrollMargin coalesces measure() into a single rAF and observes
  only wrapper + scroller + wrapper.parentElement, dropping the per-
  previous-sibling ResizeObserver chain that re-translated visible
  virtual rows on every TaskMetaSection elapsed-timer tick.
- tool-markers recognizes the harness's `[post-task_done test run: ...]`
  prose markers, so they render as paired run_command Blocks (with the
  PASSED/FAILED outcome on the same card) instead of raw bracketed text.

rawCommits.subject: Move task storage from localStorage to IndexedDB
rawCommits.body:
Phase 1 of the run-pane storage quota fix. The task subsystem
(text cache, panel rows, structured turn cache) was sharing the
~5-10 MB localStorage budget with auth/UI keys, which silently
broke session restore and persistence once long automation
transcripts filled the quota.

Move three caches to IDB stores (taskOutputCache, taskOutputPanel,
taskTurns) following the existing chatHistory exclusion pattern in
browser-db.ts. Auto-migrate the legacy localStorage keys
(aura-task-output-cache-v1, aura-task-output-panel-tasks,
aura-task-turns-v1) on first hydration after deploy so existing
stuck users are unstuck without manual action.

Read APIs become async (getCachedTaskOutputText, readTaskTurns,
hydratePanelStoreFromStorage); write APIs stay fire-and-forget
void through the existing debounce.

rawCommits.subject: Add defense-in-depth for localStorage quota exhaustion
rawCommits.body:
Phase 2 of the run-pane storage quota fix. After Phase 1 moved the
task subsystem to IndexedDB, this adds two safety nets so that if
some OTHER localStorage key ever fills the quota in the future:

1. writeSyncStoredSession catches QuotaExceededError, evicts the
   three legacy task localStorage keys (redundant with the Phase 1
   IDB stores), and retries the session/JWT write once. Auth restore
   can no longer silently die from storage pressure.

2. markStoragePressure() walks localStorage at boot and emits a
   console.warn if total usage exceeds 3 MB, including the top-5
   keys by size. Surfaces this class of issue immediately in any
   future bug report.

rawCommits.subject: [Phase A / Commit 2] Migrate to RuntimeRequest wire shape
rawCommits.body:
Mirror the new aura-protocol RuntimeRequest shape into
crates/aura-protocol (parallel to the harness side): new
runtime_request module carrying RuntimeRequest, RuntimeRequestType
{Chat, DevLoop, TaskRun}, AgentIdentity, ModelSelection,
WorkspaceLocation, ProjectContext, AgentCapabilities, plus
RuntimeRunResponse. Rename AgentIdentityWire to AgentPersona
nested inside the new AgentIdentity wrapper, regenerate the
ts-rs TypeScript bindings under crates/aura-protocol/bindings/,
delete the obsolete SessionInit.ts mirror.

Repoint aura-os-harness HTTP client + local_harness WS handshake
onto the new two-step exchange:
- AutomatonClient::start now POSTs to /v1/run with a
  RuntimeRequest body (translated from the existing
  AutomatonStartParams builder via
  automaton_start_params_to_runtime_request) and returns a
  RunHandle { run_id, event_stream_url } (renamed from
  AutomatonStartResult).
- HarnessClient::subscribe_stream takes a run_id and connects to
  /stream/:run_id.
- HarnessClient::start_automaton translates the legacy
  HarnessAutomatonStartParams scheduled-process shape onto a
  RuntimeRequest::DevLoop {} body.
- LocalHarness::open_session does POST /v1/run then opens
  WS /stream/:run_id; the previous InboundMessage::SessionInit
  first-frame send is gone. The retry / backoff loop wraps both
  steps in a single attempt.
- Rename harness::build_session_init -> build_runtime_request and
  validate_session_init_identity -> validate_runtime_request_identity.
- Lifecycle endpoints (pause / stop / resume / status) move to
  /v1/run/:id/{pause,stop,resume,status} to match the harness.

Update aura-os-server handlers + the harness_client_test mock to
serve POST /v1/run + WS /stream/:run_id instead of the bare
/stream + /automaton/start surfaces. Rename the
session_identity error tag from context: "session_init" to
"runtime_request" so the structured 422 envelope stays
consistent with the new wire-side terminology. Update the dev-loop
start / run handlers to read RunHandle.run_id rather than the
deleted AutomatonStartResult.automaton_id field.

Update interface/src/shared/types/harness-protocol.ts to drop the
{ type: "session_init" } & SessionInit arm from InboundMessage and
add the RuntimeRequest / RuntimeRequestType / AgentIdentity /
AgentPersona / ModelSelection / WorkspaceLocation / ProjectContext /
AgentCapabilities / RuntimeRunResponse shapes. Update
interface/scripts/lib/harness-session-runner.mjs::openHarnessSession
to do the two-step exchange (POST /v1/run then open
WS /stream/:run_id) and drop the toJsonMessage("session_init", ...)
send. interface/scripts/run-harness-context-benchmark.mjs picks up
the new openHarnessSession signature.

Lands back-to-back with aura-harness/main commit
"[Phase A / Commit 1] Unify session-start wire shape into
RuntimeRequest" (ce1cbaf) — both repos are now aligned on the
new wire shape.

Deviation notes:
- AutomatonStartParams was kept as an internal builder in
  aura-os-harness rather than fully removed; the new wire shape is
  produced on the HTTP send via
  automaton_start_params_to_runtime_request. Wholesale rewrite of
  every caller (start/params.rs, process_automaton.rs,
  start_or_adopt.rs) to build RuntimeRequest directly is deferred
  to a follow-up that can also drop AutomatonStartParams from the
  public API — Phase A's load-bearing goal (wire shape unification)
  is satisfied because the canonical RuntimeRequest is now what
  travels over the wire.
- Pre-existing aura-os clippy warnings (large_enum_variant on
  OutboundMessage, too_many_arguments on aura-os-ide's
  open_ide_window) are NOT introduced by this commit; aura-os HEAD
  before this commit also fails `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`.
- Pre-existing test failure
  `handlers::agents::chat::persist::pin::pin_tests::try_pin_session_matches_when_session_belongs_to_agent`
  is NOT introduced by this commit; it fails on aura-os HEAD too.
- `cargo fmt --all` touched several apps/aura-os-server files
  unrelated to Phase A because aura-os HEAD already failed
  `cargo fmt --check`. The formatting cleanup is included in this
  commit so the post-Phase-A repo passes the exit gate's fmt check.

Verified: cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --workspace
(all targets), cargo test -p aura-os-harness (-p aura-os-server
runs to completion with only the pre-existing failure noted above).

rawCommits.subject: feat(product-page): make agent card hover read as the card lifting
rawCommits.body:
The previous hover treatment scaled the card div correctly but the
result read as just the image enlarging — the card's visible
chrome (1px white inset at 6% alpha) was too faint to distinguish
the bezel from the portrait it framed, so the eye locked onto the
image growing rather than the card stepping forward. Reworks the
hover state so the entire CARD obviously lifts off the row:

- Idle inset border: 1px / 6% white -> 2px / 18% white. Always-
  visible bezel that traces the rounded corner, giving the card
  a clear edge that the eye can track as the box scales.
- Hover transform: scale(1.18) -> translateY(-8px) scale(1.25).
  Bigger inflation magnitude AND a fixed 8px lift off the row
  baseline, so the card unmistakably steps OUT of the strip
  rather than enlarging in place. Combined effect: hovered
  card's bottom edge sits ~46.5px above its row neighbors
  (`(scale-1) * height / 2 + 8`).
- Hover shadow: 24/56/0.46 -> 32/80/0.55 drop, plus the inset
  border brightens to 38% white so the focused card's bezel
  pops against the now full-color portrait.
- Gaps recalculated for the bigger 1.25 scale: 40 -> 52 desktop,
  30 -> 42 at 768px, 22 -> 32 at 480px. All three preserve the
  >=8px clearance floor between scaled card edge and neighbors
  via `(scale - 1) * card_w / 2 + 8px` minimum + headroom.
- Marquee duration comment updated for the new track width

the left + right edges back to the orb video. The mask is applied

vertically to comfortably contain the hovered card's overflow at
every breakpoint. The marquee remains flex-centered inside
`.pageHeroVideoOverlay`, so the visible row of cards stays
aligned to the orb's bright spot; the padding just adds a hidden
buffer above and below for the zoom to inflate into.

flat in the Y direction, so the new padded box paints the same
horizontal fade pattern over the full taller area.

rawCommits.subject: feat(mode-toggle): restore last app+item URL when flipping Simple <-> Advanced
rawCommits.body:
Track two independent localStorage paths -- `aura-last-simple-path`
(the most recent `/chat...` URL, preserving session/agent query
params) and `aura-last-advanced-path` (the most recent non-chat URL,
preserving app + item) -- and have `ModeToggle` navigate to the
appropriate stored path on flip so the user lands back on the surface
they had selected in the destination mode.

Writes happen in `AppProviders.AppSync` on every location change,
keyed off the URL itself rather than the live store mode so a brief
mode-flip window can never misclassify the path. Storage setters
validate (Simple must be `/chat...`, Advanced must not be) so a
hand-edited / stale entry can't drive `navigate()` to an invalid
surface. `setMode` is dispatched in the same handler as `navigate`,
so React batches the re-render and the destination route resolves in
one frame -- no flash of `/chat` on Simple -> Advanced.

`isChatPath` is hoisted into `last-app-path` as `isChatPathname` so
the route guard and the storage helpers share a single rule without
a components -> utils import; the original export is preserved for
existing call sites and tests.

rawCommits.subject: feat(reconnect): sequenced /ws/events firehose with replay on reconnect
rawCommits.body:
Phase 1 of intelligent reconnect. Adds a bounded, sequenced EventLog
behind the legacy event_broadcast firehose so the /ws/events forwarder
can replay missed events when a client reconnects, instead of silently
dropping everything sent during the gap.

Server:
- New EventLog (monotonic seq + bounded ring + live fan-out), fed by a
  bridge task draining event_broadcast; existing producers are untouched.
- /ws/events accepts ?since=<seq>, replays the buffered backlog (de-duped
  against the live stream), and emits ws_resync_required when the caller
  fell too far behind the ring.
- Each forwarded frame is stamped with its seq.

Client:
- event-store tracks lastSeq and sends ?since= on every reconnect via a
  per-attempt URL function; handles ws_resync_required by re-snapshotting
  authoritative HTTP state.
- use-task-output-view rehydrates in-flight task output (not just
  terminal) while the firehose is connected and the stream store is empty.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: sequenced /ws/events firehose with replay on reconnect

rawCommits.subject: feat(reconnect): resumable harness stream registry + /api/streams
rawCommits.body:
Phase 2 of intelligent reconnect. Introduces the server-side primitives
and client SSE plumbing for reattaching to in-flight harness runs.

Server:
- LiveStreamRegistry decouples a HarnessSession's lifetime from the SSE
  response. A forwarder task pumps harness frames into a per-stream
  sequenced EventLog and holds the session alive until a terminal frame;
  terminated streams linger for a TTL (sweeper-reaped) so a client that
  reconnects just after completion still gets the tail.
- New endpoints (protected): GET /api/streams/active (list reattachable
  streams scoped to the caller), GET /api/streams/:id (SSE replay from
  ?since=<seq> then live, stamping each frame's seq as the SSE id, with
  typed stream_heartbeat), POST /api/streams/:id/cancel.

Client:
- streamSSE parses the SSE id: field and gains opt-in resume: a
  recoverable close (idle timeout / transport drop, not HTTP error or
  abort) re-issues the request with ?since=<lastId> and resumes the same
  onEvent stream. Only for idempotent GET attach endpoints.

No existing flow is migrated onto the registry yet; that is Phase 3.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: resumable harness stream registry + /api/streams

rawCommits.subject: feat(reconnect): migrate streaming spec generation onto the stream registry
rawCommits.body:
Phase 3 (spec gen) of intelligent reconnect. The streaming spec-gen
endpoint no longer owns the HarnessSession inside its SSE unfold;
instead it registers the session with the LiveStreamRegistry and serves
the shared resumable SSE body (replay-from-seq + heartbeat).

- /api/projects/:id/specs/generate/stream registers a SpecGen stream
  scoped to (user, project, agent instance) and returns the new
  X-Aura-Attach-Id header so the client can reattach.
- The run now survives a dropped SSE connection: the harness keeps
  generating and a reconnecting/reloaded client can rediscover the run
  via GET /api/streams/active and reattach with ?since=<seq> instead of
  restarting generation.
- Removes the bespoke harness_specs_to_sse unfold in favour of the
  registry-backed attach_sse.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: migrate streaming spec generation onto the stream registry

rawCommits.subject: feat(reconnect): client stream-reattach API, registry tests, env knobs
rawCommits.body:
Phase 4 (client building blocks) + Phase 5 (tests, config) of
intelligent reconnect.

Client:
- shared/api/streams.ts: listActiveStreams / cancelStream against the

- api/streams.ts: attachToStream() reattaches to a registered stream via

Server / config:

- Documented AURA_EVENT_LOG_CAPACITY / AURA_STREAM_LOG_CAPACITY /

Remaining (follow-up): migrating the chat / image / video / 3D SSE flows

rawCommits.subject: fix(tasks): flip task modal off "in progress" on tool-driven completion
rawCommits.body:
The task modal/preview reads live status only from the per-task
live-status store, which was written exclusively by the harness
lifecycle handlers. When an agent completes a task via a tool call,
the server emits a `task_updated` { from, to } status edge with no
harness `task_completed` event, and `handleTaskUpdated` discarded it
for status edges. The modal therefore stayed "In Progress" with a
"Cooking..." indicator until a manual refresh.

Mirror the status edge's `to` value into the live-status store while
still suppressing the duplicate transition block, so every
`useTaskStatus` consumer (task modal/preview, RunTaskButton) reacts
to tool-driven status changes live.

rawCommits.subject: feat(dev-loop): surface tool command and result in automation logs
rawCommits.body:
The aura::automation logs recorded only the tool name, so a run_command
that runs to the hard 120s per-tool timeout showed as an opaque
tool=run_command line with no command and no failure text - making a
tool-timeout retry loop impossible to diagnose from logs.

Add a shared tool_summary helper that pulls a bounded summary from the
event payload the harness already sends, and wire it into:
- the "automation tool call started" trace line (input summary)
- the "automation tool call completed" line (input, duration_ms, result)

rawCommits.body:
Phase 3a of unifying the harness transports (additive; AutomatonClient
still present, build green; 105 harness tests pass).

- HarnessLink gains submit_run (POST /v1/run -> RunHandle, mapping 409 ->
  Conflict{run_id} and 503 -> CapacityExhausted) and attach_run(run_id,
  wait_for_ready) plus run-lifecycle (pause_run/stop_run/run_status), all
  with default "unsupported" impls so the swarm transport and test fakes
  compile unchanged. LocalHarness implements them by splitting the old
  try_open_session_attempt into submit_run_once + attach_run_once; chat
  waits for SessionReady, automaton runs use a liveness probe and use
  run_id as the session id.
- RunHandle + a Conflict error variant move into the harness/error core;
  409 conflict run_id extraction is ported for the dev-loop adopt path.
- ws_bridge now publishes the complete normalized JSON Value for EVERY
  frame on raw_events_tx (not just typed-parse misses), so a raw-only
  automaton consumer sharing this single bridge sees every event. Chat
  consumers read the typed channel and are unaffected.

This is the canonical transport surface that the automaton consumers and
AutomatonClient will be migrated onto next.

rawCommits.body:
Add update_spec_section and append_to_spec endpoints/tools that read-modify-
write a single `## ` section or append a block server-side, so agents stop
re-emitting the whole spec body on every edit. Spec writes now return a
blake3 content_hash and accept an if_match token that refuses stale updates
with HTTP 409. Broaden update_task tool to expose order_index and
dependency_ids. Wires the new tools through the shared tool schema, the MCP
sidecar, the harness-native dedupe list, and UI labels.

rawCommits.body:
Dev-loop tasks are marked done by the agent calling a transition tool,
which broadcasts a `task_updated` status edge (in_progress -> done)
rather than a harness `task_completed` lifecycle event. The Run pane and
Tasks tab only consumed the lifecycle events, so finished rows lingered
as "in progress" until a manual refresh refetched `/tasks` and ran
`reconcileStatuses`.

Route terminal `task_updated` edges into the Run pane panel store (via
shared finalize helpers extracted from the completed/failed handlers)
and into the Tasks tab list state so both surfaces update live.

rawCommits.subject: harness: migrate automaton runner onto canonical HarnessLink transport
rawCommits.body:
Phase 3b of the harness-transport unification. The shared automaton
runner and the WS-reader handle now ride the canonical HarnessLink
surface (`submit_run` + `attach_run_at_url`) instead of the bespoke
`AutomatonClient::connect_event_stream` reader task.

- Relocate `WsReaderHandle` out of `automaton_client` into a top-level
  module and reimplement it to OWN a `HarnessSession`: `cancel()` /
  last-clone `Drop` take the session, dropping `commands_tx` so the
  ws-bridge writer closes the socket and releases the harness ws slot.
  Public name / `cancel` / `clone` / `Debug` preserved.
- Add `attach_run_at_url` (event_stream_url with absolute/relative/None
  resolution), `resume_run`, and `resolve_workspace` to `HarnessLink`
  with default-unsupported impls, implemented on `LocalHarness`.
- Add typed `HarnessError::UpstreamStatus` / `Unreachable` causes plus
  `conflict_run_id` / `upstream_status` / `unreachable_cause` helpers;
  `submit_run_once` now threads connect/timeout and non-409/503 status
  through these so the dev-loop start taxonomy survives.
- Migrate the runner: new `submit_automaton_run` maps submit errors back
  onto `AutomatonStartError`; `start_and_connect` / `connect_with_retries`
  take `&dyn HarnessLink` + `auth_token` and build the session-backed
  `WsReaderHandle` from `raw_events_tx`.
- Collapse the duplicate `start_params::RunHandle` onto `harness::RunHandle`;
  drop `AutomatonClient::connect_event_stream` and the now-dead
  `ws_reader` / `ws_reader_handle` modules. `AutomatonClient` retains its
  lifecycle methods until its server consumers migrate.

rawCommits.subject: server: migrate dev-loop / process automaton consumers onto HarnessLink
rawCommits.body:
Phase 4 of the harness-transport unification. The dev-loop and
scheduled-process paths now drive the canonical `HarnessLink` surface
instead of the bespoke `AutomatonClient`, and `AppState` drops the
dedicated `automaton_client` field.

- `StartContext` now carries `client: Arc<dyn HarnessLink>` plus the
  `harness_base_url` / `harness_auth_token` it needs (the trait is
  transport-only, with no `base_url()` accessor). Both modes ride
  `LocalHarness` (POST /v1/run + WS /stream): local shares
  `state.local_harness` with no bearer (identity in the body, matching
  the old no-auth client); swarm builds a per-request transport against
  the gateway `/v1/agents/:id` base bearing the JWT.
- `start_or_adopt` / single-task start use `submit_automaton_run` and the
  `run_status` / `stop_run` lifecycle calls; the conflict / capacity /
  connect-timeout / structured-status taxonomy and the
  `service_unavailable + ensure_local_harness_running` UX are preserved.
- `connect_automaton_stream` threads the auth token into the migrated
  `connect_with_retries`; the registry stores `harness_base_url` from the
  start context.
- `control.rs` / `credits.rs` rebuild a `LocalHarness` from the stored
  base URL and call `pause_run` / `resume_run` / `stop_run` (resume maps
  to POST /v1/run/:id/resume, matching the old client). `resolve_workspace`
  moves onto the `HarnessLink` trait.
- `process_automaton` builds its `HarnessClient` from
  `local_harness_base_url()`; drop `state.automaton_client` and every
  constructor site (app_builder, billing test state, auth_guard tests,
  integration test harness).

rawCommits.body:
Final step of the harness-transport unification. With every consumer
migrated onto `HarnessLink`, the bespoke `AutomatonClient` HTTP/WS
client is dead code.

- Delete `automaton_client/client.rs` and drop the `AutomatonClient`
  re-export; the `automaton_client` module now only hosts the
  request-shaping (`AutomatonStartParams` → `RuntimeRequest`) and
  identity-preflight helpers the dev-loop start path still uses.
- Port the conflict-id extraction coverage from the removed
  `client.rs` parser tests onto `LocalHarness::extract_conflict_run_id`

  free-text substring / missing-id shapes).
- Refresh the now-stale `validate_automaton_start_identity` doc link to
  point at the canonical `HarnessLink::submit_run` path.

rawCommits.subject: harness: stop flagging expected automaton events as protocol mismatch
rawCommits.body:
The shared WS bridge parses every harness frame against the typed chat
protocol (OutboundMessage). Automaton/dev-loop events (token_usage,
tool_call_completed, debug.*, git/sync milestones) are intentionally
absent from that enum and flow on the raw channel, so the failed typed
parse was logged as a WARN, bumped the harness_protocol_mismatch metric,
and emitted a synthetic error the client treats as a stream drop.

Add is_known_raw_only_event() and short-circuit those frames in the
bridge: log at debug and skip the metric + typed error. Genuinely
unknown frames keep the warn + protocol-mismatch behavior.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: harness: stop flagging expected automaton events as protocol mismatch

rawCommits.subject: protocol: classify automaton events via typed AutomatonEvent enum
rawCommits.body:
Replace the hand-maintained is_known_raw_only_event allowlist in the
harness with a forward-compatible AutomatonEvent enum in aura-protocol.
It is internally tagged on `type` with a #[serde(other)] Unknown
catch-all, so the WS bridge classifies expected automaton/dev-loop
frames (token_usage, tool_call_completed, git/sync, debug.*) without a
manually-curated list that can drift from harness output. Unrecognized
tags fall to Unknown and keep the warn + harness_protocol_mismatch
behavior, preserving detection of genuine protocol drift.

The open debug.* instrumentation namespace is matched by prefix in
is_recognized() since an internally-tagged enum cannot express it as
fixed variants.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: protocol: classify automaton events via typed AutomatonEvent enum

rawCommits.subject: feat(reconnect): LiveStreamRegistry::register_receiver for unowned chat streams
rawCommits.body:
Add LiveStreamRegistry::register_receiver, which pumps an
already-subscribed broadcast::Receiver<HarnessOutbound> into a
per-stream EventLog WITHOUT owning the underlying HarnessSession. Chat
turns reuse a session that lives in chat_sessions, so the live stream
must observe the turn's frames without holding (and on completion
dropping/closing) the shared session.

- Extract the forwarder body into a shared spawn_forwarder() so the
  owned-session (register) and unowned-receiver (register_receiver)
  paths stay in lockstep on terminal detection (AssistantMessageEnd /
  Error / cancel / upstream close) and TTL retention.
- Add LiveStream.cancel_tx: Option<HarnessCommandSender>. cancel() now
  also forwards HarnessInbound::Cancel over it (new behavior; cancel
  was previously token-only). None for the owned-session register path,
  where dropping the session is sufficient. Required because dropping an
  unowned session cannot abort the upstream turn.
- session: Mutex::new(None) for the receiver path; mark_terminated()
  no-ops on the empty session field.
- Add unit tests for the receiver path: forwarder records frames + marks
  terminal, scope listing/filtering, and cancel forwards Cancel.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: LiveStreamRegistry::register_receiver for unowned chat streams

rawCommits.subject: feat(reconnect): register each chat turn as a reattachable stream
rawCommits.body:
In open_harness_chat_stream, register a ChatTurn live stream right after
the SessionForTurn destructure and before the persist/release/watchdog
fan-out. The stream subscribes a FRESH events_tx.subscribe() receiver
(not the SSE body's `rx`) so the registry observes the turn's frames
without stealing them, and passes commands_tx so an explicit cancel can
abort the upstream turn.

This lets a reconnecting / reloading UI rejoin the in-flight delta
stream by session_id via GET /api/streams/active + GET /api/streams/:id.
The turn slot serializes turns on the reused events_tx, so the forwarder
captures exactly one turn and terminates at its assistant_message_end.
Plan-mode spec-gen issued over chat is registered as ChatTurn too
(intended).

Scope:
- user_id from session_config.user_id (authz-load-bearing in
  streams::authorize; reliably set at both chat routes), snapshotted
  before session_config is moved into the session resolver.
- project_id from session_config, falling back to ctx.project_id.
- agent_instance_id = 2nd "::"-segment of session_key
  (template::instance::session), None when absent.
- session_id from ctx.session_id.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: register each chat turn as a reattachable stream

rawCommits.subject: fix(loops): clear task pointer + finalize stream on tool-driven completion
rawCommits.body:
Single-task runs and dev-loop automation both complete a task via the
agent's transition_task / update_task tool, which emits only a
task_updated status edge -- never a harness task_completed / task_failed
lifecycle event. The "task finished" cleanup was wired only to those
lifecycle events, so the loop kept advertising the finished task as its
current_task_id and the task's live stream kept isStreaming set. Result:
per-task spinners, the "Cooking" indicator, and the "In Progress" status
lingered until a manual refresh re-hydrated GET /api/loops / re-fetched
tasks.

Server: add LoopRegistry::clear_current_task(project, task_id) and call
it from the HTTP transition handlers (transition_task, update_task)
whenever a task goes terminal (Done/Failed). It compare-and-clears (only
loops still bound to that task, so a concurrent task_started rebinding
the next task is never clobbered) and publishes LoopActivityChanged so
loop-activity-derived UI settles live. Both run modes drive completion
through these endpoints, so this shared chokepoint covers both.

Client: handleTaskUpdated now finalizes the task stream on any terminal
status edge regardless of whether the Run pane already has a row, so a
previewed-but-unpinned task clears its live "Cooking" / Live Output
block (finalizeStream flips isStreaming off; complete/failTask are
no-ops for unknown ids and stay idempotent).

Tests: 3 new registry tests (clears + publishes, no-clobber on rebind,
project-scoped) and a frontend test (terminal task_updated finalizes
the stream with no Run pane row).
rawCommits.cleanSubject: clear task pointer + finalize stream on tool-driven completion

rawCommits.subject: fix(reconnect): keep harness turn alive on passive SSE disconnect
rawCommits.body:
A passive SSE disconnect (the UI closed the response body on a browser
refresh or network drop) previously cancelled the harness turn and
early-released the per-partition turn slot via the SSE drop guard. That
defeats reattach: the reused harness turn must keep running so a
reconnecting / reloading UI can rejoin its registered live stream.

Behavior change (load-bearing):
- Remove the SSE drop guard and its early-release oneshot from
  open_harness_chat_stream. Delete streaming/drop_guard.rs (now dead).
- spawn_turn_slot_release now releases the turn slot SOLELY on the
  harness terminal event (AssistantMessageEnd / Error) or broadcast
  close. Its signature drops the early_release_rx parameter.

Why this is safe for turn-slot accounting:
- A genuinely stalled turn is still bounded by spawn_turn_watchdog,
  which emits a synthetic terminal event on first-event / idle timeout;
  the sentinel observes it on the same broadcast, so the slot can never
  leak indefinitely even if the harness goes silent after a disconnect.
- The reused harness session lives in chat_sessions independently of the
  SSE body, so the turn keeps producing frames (now captured by the
  ChatTurn live stream) and reaches a terminal event normally.

Why explicit Stop still cancels:
- POST .../cancel-turn (setup/cancel.rs) forwards HarnessInbound::Cancel
  to the live session's command channel and evicts the warm session.
  That path is fully independent of the SSE body and unchanged here; the
  harness then emits a terminal event that spawn_turn_slot_release
  observes, releasing the slot promptly. The registered live stream's
  cancel() also forwards Cancel for explicit registry-level cancels.

Tests:
- release.rs: replace the early-release tests with a regression guard
  (spawn_turn_slot_release_holds_slot_until_terminal_event) proving the
  slot stays held while only non-terminal frames arrive and releases on
  the terminal event.
- Update the three terminal-event release tests to the 2-arg signature.
- cancel.rs tests (explicit Stop) remain green and unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: keep harness turn alive on passive SSE disconnect

rawCommits.subject: feat(reconnect): reattach in-flight chat turn on reconnect/reload
rawCommits.body:
Part B of the chat reconnect/reattach work. A reconnecting or
hard-reloading UI now rejoins the in-flight chat (and chat-driven
spec-gen) turn the server keeps alive (Part A) by reattaching to its
registered ChatTurn stream and feeding the SAME chat stream handler, so
deltas / tool cards / thinking render seamlessly.

- shared/api/sse: expose an optional `onSeq(seq)` from streamSSE so
  callers can persist the SSE `id:` cursor.
- api/streams: `attachToStream` now accepts `{ onSeq, onResync }` and
  intercepts the server `stream_resync_required` control frame (so it is
  not mis-parsed as a chat event); add pure `selectReattachableChatStream`
  selection helper (matches live, non-terminated `chat_turn` by session).
- partition-state: add `activeAttachId` / `attachLastSeq` /
  `reattaching` to PartitionSendControl + `getIsReattaching` latch.
- use-chat-stream: `tryReattachActiveTurn()` reused by (a) a mount /
  session-pin effect (hard-reload) and (b) the auto-retry path, where it
  runs before the re-POST fallback. Dedup-safe: only fires on a clean
  partition buffer, so a replay-from-cursor cannot double-apply rendered
  content. Tracks `attachLastSeq` via the `onSeq` callback; handles
  `stream_resync_required` by clearing buffers and letting the post-stream
  history refetch converge.
- use-chat-history-sync: gate the firehose-driven refetch on the
  `reattaching` latch so it cannot reset events[] mid-reattach.
- use-agent-chat-stream: mirror the reattach for standalone agent chat
  (match purely on session_id; omit agent_instance_id).
- tests: selection logic, attachToStream resync/onSeq interception, and
  streamSSE onSeq reporting.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): land cross-agent messages in the session the UI opens
rawCommits.body:
Cross-agent sends (CEO -> Barret via send_to_agent) POST with no
session_id, so the write resolved its target via matching.first()
binding and its latest session. The recipient's chat UI, however,
opens the globally most-recent session by started_at across ALL of
the agent's bindings (findMostRecentRealSession / sortSessionsDesc).
When those bindings differed, the message persisted
(x-aura-chat-persisted: true) yet the panel rendered empty even after
a reload, and the live WS user_message event never matched the open
panel's watched session.

Mirror the UI's default-session selection on the server: for unpinned,
non-force_new writes, pick the binding that owns the globally newest
session across all bindings. This realigns persistence with both the
session-scoped history read and the WS-driven live refetch, so the
recipient sees the message in real time and after refresh. The B->A
reply callback flows through the same path, so threaded replies land in
the originator's UI-visible session too.

Also surface a silent failure mode on the reply leg: verify the
x-aura-chat-persisted header on the callback response and warn when the
originating session did not persist the reply (e.g. missing binding),
instead of treating any 2xx as success.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: feat(chat): add Retry button to error bubbles
rawCommits.body:
When a turn fails (server busy, agent busy, or a generic stream error),
the error bubble now shows a manual Retry button that resends the most
recent prompt by reusing the existing last-send replay logic that powers
the stuck-stream pill. Threaded through ChatPanel -> ChatMessageList ->
MessageBubble, so desktop, standalone-agent, and mobile surfaces all get
it. The insufficient-credits variant is excluded (keeps Buy credits).

rawCommits.subject: fix(cross-agent): carry the turn model on the reply callback
rawCommits.body:
The B->A cross-agent reply callback POSTed model: null, so when the
originating agent had no server-side configured model, its
reply-triggered turn opened with an empty model and failed with "model
name must not be empty".

Thread the model the replying agent's turn ran on (persist_model, in
scope in run_persist_loop) into spawn_cross_agent_reply_callback and
emit it as "model" on the callback POST. Combined with the harness
forwarding the caller's model on the A->B leg, the whole cross-agent
thread now stays on a single real model.

rendered.title: AuraShell unification, public landing rebuild, and dev-loop reliability overhaul
rendered.intro: A very large nightly that consolidates the desktop and logged-out shells into a single AuraShell, rebuilds the public landing around persona-themed mock desktops and a refreshed marketing surface, and lands a deep simplification of the dev-loop, harness transport, and task streaming pipeline. Reliability work covers Start/Stop wedges, reattachable chat and task streams, IndexedDB-backed task storage, and a long string of UI fixes for the sidekick Run pane and activity timeline.

entries.title: AuraShell unification and public landing rebuild
entries.summary: Collapsed DesktopShell and LoggedOutShell into a single AuraShell mounted once, unified Simple/Advanced/Public modes behind one ui-mode-store, and rebuilt the logged-out surface around persona-themed mock desktops, marketing pages, and a refreshed chrome.

items.text: Consolidated DesktopShell and LoggedOutShell into one AuraShell with stable DOM identity across Simple/Advanced/Public flips, plus a new ui-mode-store that migrates legacy Normie users to Simple and pins ChatApp in Simple mode.

Rebuilt the public landing as a persona-driven hero: right-edge PersonaTickRail and bottom avatar dock both drive a layered cross-fade between persona wallpapers, page backgrounds, CTA glow, and nav contrast tokens, with mouse-wheel cycling and curated themes for Vibecoder, Solo Builder, Giga Brain, Coordinator, Researcher, and Cypher Punk.

Replaced the old empty-state banner with a windowed MockAuraApp hero: real ShellTitlebar overlay, BottomTaskbar-style dock pills, fish-eye magnified persona dock, and four MSN-style DM windows with expand/staggered-collapse, FLIP scrolling, syntax-highlighted code, and theme-derived chat palettes.

Routed Product, Changelog, Feedback, Pricing, and Models into a PublicMarketingPanel that mounts inside the public shell, ported aura-web's /feedback proxy onto aura-os-server, and added a Download pill plus auto-detected installer link from the changelog Current Version stat.

Polished the public chrome: shimmering neon 'Create your agent' CTA, sliding active pill in the marketing nav, persona-aware sidebar text, sliding Simple/Advanced toggle, and a Powered-by-THE-GRID lightning bolt in the public bottom taskbar.
Added a mobile public shell with hamburger drawer and chat composer so logged-out visitors on iOS/Android get a proper public surface instead of falling through to the authed MobileShell.

Reworked the dev-loop pipeline: collapsed three completion gates into a single workspace-health rule, replaced in-memory retry trackers with a persisted tasks.attempts column, deleted the aura-os-automation crate, and consolidated start_loop/run_single behind a shared RunRequest controller.

Fixed long-standing dev-loop wedges: synchronous LoopEnded on Stop, freshness gate on forwarder reuse, attempt-aware retry policy for ResearchLoopAbort, and a client safety-net hydrate after every Start/Resume/Stop.

Sidekick Run pane and Tasks tab finally bind to live automation: forwarder events stamp routing fields, implicit task_started is synthesized when the harness skips it, and the per-task context-usage pill hydrates from a new endpoint so cold-loaded rows show their context ring.

Tightened the chat input experience: anti-oscillation lockout at the wrap boundary, copy button unified across every Block renderer, per-segment thinking durations, session-wide gallery navigation, and a fade-in for decoded images.

Reliability and platform plumbing: per-token aura-network sync dedupe, persisted sentinel that silences the permissions heal storm across restarts, repo-local Cargo target dir, and structured planning contracts for specs and tasks.

entries.title: Image generation: deliver completion frame before storage persistence
entries.summary: Fixed an image-generation hang where a slow storage backend could prevent the terminal SSE frame from ever reaching the client.

items.text: Reordered run_image_upstream_task so the generation_completed SSE frame is sent before persist_completion is awaited, preventing the client from sitting on a forever-cooking pill when storage is slow or unreachable; persistence still runs best-effort afterward and a new regression test pins the timing.

entries.title: Reattachable streams, IndexedDB task storage, and RuntimeRequest wire shape
entries.summary: Migrated the harness session-start onto a single RuntimeRequest wire, introduced sequenced firehose and per-stream live registries so chat and task streams survive reloads, moved task caches off localStorage to IndexedDB, and polished the activity timeline.

items.text: Migrated session start to a unified RuntimeRequest two-step exchange (POST /v1/run then WS /stream/:run_id) across the harness client, local harness, and aura-os-server handlers, deprecating the old SessionInit first-frame contract.

Added a sequenced /ws/events firehose with replay on reconnect, a LiveStreamRegistry for resumable per-run SSE, and migrated streaming spec generation onto the registry so a dropped connection no longer restarts generation.

Moved task output cache, panel store, and turn cache from localStorage to IndexedDB with auto-migration, plus a boot diagnostic that warns on >3MB localStorage usage and an auth-restore retry that evicts legacy task keys on QuotaExceededError.

Stabilized the sidekick task preview during live streaming: virtualized timeline and event list with @tanstack/react-virtual, deferred trailing tool cards while text streams, restored prior assistant turns above the live stream, and recognized post-task_done test markers.

Restored visible thinking blocks during streaming, collapsed empty Thinking placeholders to header-only rows, and rolled out a synthetic Brain Thinking block for models that don't emit thinking_delta so every standard LLM surface shows reasoning narration consistently.

Marketing surfaces gained a /models page proxied through aura-os-server, a floating changelog stats card with live commit counts from seven GitHub repos and a releases-per-day chart, a /product agent marquee with hover-zoom posters, and an AgentChatSection with three overlapping phone shells.
Polished public assets: replaced placeholder iOS app icon with the AURA orb and unblocked mobile chat input for local agents.
Restored readable task descriptions in dark mode, kept the streaming caret mounted to avoid 1px text shifts on completion, and preserved live output across refresh during active runs.

entries.title: Automation tool logging and canonical HarnessSession run_id
entries.summary: Surfaced tool command and result text in aura::automation logs and started consolidating the harness transport behind a single canonical run abstraction.

items.text: Automation traces now record the tool command summary, duration, and result on tool_call_started/completed, including the failure text on errors, so a run_command timeout is finally diagnosable from logs alone.

HarnessSession now retains the harness-allocated run_id and exposes a canonical open_run plus run_id-keyed pause/stop/status, with shared git-event normalization on the unified ws_bridge so every consumer gets canonical git event shapes.

entries.title: Clearer tool feedback in the sidekick activity timeline
entries.summary: Tightened the streaming UX so command rows, phase labels, and the Thinking placeholder reflect what's actually happening during tool runs.

items.text: CommandBlock now distinguishes in-flight, clean-exit, and empty-output states instead of always saying 'No output', the pinned phase label stops reporting stale Thinking once tools have run, and a new tool_call_started settles prior still-pending rows so the timeline shows one active row at a time.

entries.title: Resumable chat turns, granular spec edits, and unified HarnessLink transport
entries.summary: Completed the harness transport unification on HarnessLink, made chat turns survive passive SSE disconnects and reattach on reload, added granular spec-edit tools with if_match concurrency, and finished a string of cross-agent and task-state fixes.

items.text: Migrated every automaton and dev-loop consumer onto the canonical HarnessLink transport (submit_run/attach_run) and deleted the legacy AutomatonClient, so chat and automaton runs now share one HTTP/WS surface with typed AutomatonEvent classification on the bridge.

Each chat turn is now registered as a reattachable ChatTurn stream and the client reattaches in-flight turns on reload or transient disconnect via /api/streams, with passive SSE drops no longer cancelling the upstream turn.

Added granular update_spec_section and append_to_spec endpoints/tools with blake3 content_hash plus if_match concurrency so agents stop re-emitting whole spec bodies and stale edits fail loudly with 409.
Tool-driven task completions now flip the task modal off In Progress, clear the loop's current_task_id, and finalize the per-task stream live, instead of waiting for a manual refresh.

Chat got user-facing recovery affordances: a Retry button on error bubbles, a moving placeholder while images and videos generate, and the overlay scrollbar lifted above the input fade so the thumb stays visible.

Fixed cross-agent messaging so replies land in the session the recipient UI actually opens and the B->A callback carries the turn's model, eliminating empty-panel and 'model name must not be empty' regressions.
Suppressed the warn + protocol-mismatch noise that automaton-only frames produced on the shared WS bridge by classifying them through a typed AutomatonEvent enum with an Unknown catch-all.

highlights: One unified AuraShell across Simple, Advanced, and Public modes
Rebuilt public landing with persona theming, mock Aura desktop, and marketing pages
Dev-loop simplified: one health gate, persisted attempts, unified HarnessLink transport
Reattachable chat and task streams survive reloads and SSE drops
Sidekick Run pane and activity timeline finally show live task progress reliably
Task storage moved off localStorage to IndexedDB to end quota wedges
